News.title: ‘Multiple people injured’ after suspect armed with sword storms school in Sweden sparking lockdown
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SWORD ATTACK ‘Multiple people injured’ after suspect armed with sword storms school in Sweden sparking lockdown

SEVERAL people have been injured after a sword-wielding suspect stormed a school in Sweden, police said.

Eight schools are now on lockdown after cops swarmed the scene in Fagersta, an industrial town around 100 miles west of Stockholm.



The suspect was reportedly shot in the leg by cops and taken into custody.

“A call was received regarding a case of ongoing deadly violence at a school in Fagersta,” police said in a statement.



“Police have responded to the scene and one person has been taken into custody.

“Police are continuing to work at the scene with a number of different resources.



“The public is urged to respect the roadblocks and listen to police instructions.”

Minister of Justice Gunnar Strömmer told Aftonbladet: “We have been informed of a serious incident in Fagersta.

“The police are on site and are working very intensively on the incident.

“The government is in close contact with the police and is continuously monitoring developments.”

News.title: Boy, 14, killed after being hit by bus outside city centre train station is pictured – as family pay poignant tribute
News.content:
'OUR DARLING BOY' Boy, 14, killed after being hit by bus outside city centre train station is pictured – as family pay poignant tribute

A 14-YEAR-OLD boy who died after being hit by a bus outside a city centre train station has been pictured for the first time.

Beau Croucher was rushed to hospital with life-threatening injuries after a crash in Portsmouth on August 17, cops said.



The Portsmouth FC fan tragically passed away despite the best efforts of paramedics.

A 39-year-old bus driver has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving.



He has been released on bail until November 17 while further enquiries are being carried out.

Beau’s family said: “On Monday, Beau went out for the afternoon. He never came home. Right now, all of our love, our focus and our entire world is Beau.

“These are the stories you hear about and think, that could never happen to us. You never, in a million years, imagine that something so unimaginable could happen to your perfect little family.

“There are no words that can come close to describing the magnitude of the pain we are living with. It is beyond anything we ever knew was possible to feel. Our hearts are broken in a way we didn’t know a heart could break.

“Beau is our absolute world. Our heartbeat. Our obsession. Our beautiful, innocent baby boy. To know Beau was to love him. When you got to spend time with Beau it was a privilege.

“He had a unique way of making people laugh. His humour was effortless, his observations were always on point, and he brought joy and laughter to everyone who knew him.



“Beau loved going on holiday, it was only last week that we were all enjoying being together in London for his birthday and then Cornwall, where he loved to spend time with his family. He always showed gratitude for the life he lived.

“Beau was like sunshine, his light was so strong, and he always stood out in a crowd. It’s like we were blessed with an angel. It’s difficult for us to truly explain how much he meant to everyone and what an incredible boy he was.”

The force has asked for any witnesses with information, CCTV or dashcam footage to call 101 quoting reference 44260399748.

One family friend of the schoolboy posted on Facebook: “Such a great young man with so much to live for. A true credit to his family.

“Rest in eternal peace. Sending love to your whole family. We will never forget you sweetheart.”



A Hampshire Constabulary spokesman previously said: “We are appealing for information and witnesses as a young boy has died following a bus crash in Portsmouth.

At about 4.25pm on Monday August 17, police were called to The Hard after reports of a serious collision involving a pedestrian and a bus.

Cops said: “The pedestrian, a 14-year-old boy from Portsmouth, was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries and has since sadly passed away.

“His family are being supported by specialist officers.”

The force added: “The driver of the bus, a 39-year-old man from Portsmouth, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and then released on bail until November 17 while further inquiries are carried out.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Stagecoach spokesperson said: “We can confirm that one of our bus drivers was involved in a collision with a pedestrian in Portsmouth yesterday, which resulted in the pedestrian sustaining injuries.

“We are cooperating fully with Hampshire Constabulary and the local authorities, who are leading the investigation. As the matter is ongoing, it would not be appropriate for us to comment further at this stage.”

News.title: Prince Harry & celeb pals hit with first court bill of £9.5m after failed hacking case – ahead of return to UK
News.content:
PRINCE Harry and his high-profile pals are facing a first court bill of £9.5million after losing their failed hacking case with the Daily Mail’s publisher.

The Duke of Sussex, 41, was one of seven complainants – including Sir Elton John and actress Liz Hurley – who lost the battle with Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL).



The group, which also includes campaigner Baroness Doreen Lawrence, claimed journalists hired private investigators to put listening devices in cars, blag private records and tap into private phone conversations.

ANL strongly denied the allegations and argued the cases had been brought too late.



Harry and the other claimants have now been saddled with an initial court bill for £9.5million – with more set to come.

ANL is trying to claw back legal costs worth more than £34.5million but the amount the seven famous faces will need to cough up has not yet been decided.

Today’s amount is an interim payment – with the court ruling the publisher can seek further costs.

Judge Mr Justice Nicklin said the claims were were “speculative and substantially inferential” and “lacked a proper evidential foundation”.

In a huge victory for Press freedom, the judge last month rejected every single one of the 97 allegations made by the Duke and his pals.

He said the complainants had failed to prove their “serious” allegations of unlawful information gathering.



Harry later slammed the judgement as “a complete and obvious whitewash”.

But lawyers for the publisher said Harry’s team “abused their celebrity status” to pursue a case “well outside the law” and that their conduct had been “outrageous” and “unreasonable”.

Today’s judgment comes after The Sun revealed how Harry and wife Meghan Markle will be returning to the UK – six years after Megxit.



Both seven-year-old Archie and Lilibet, five, are set to go to school in the UK in September.

Prince William and Princess Kate were today pictured arriving at Balmoral where a secret summit is taking place with the royal family over Harry and Meghan’s shock return.

It echoes the Sandringham Summit in 2020 when the Sussexes first announced they wanted to leave.



During around two hours of cross-examination in January, Harry said he could not complain about some of the 14 articles in his case at the time “because of the institution I was in”.

He also said in his written evidence that “knowingly false” information was added to stories to “put me off the scent”, to conceal unlawful methods, including voicemail interception.

The duke, who flew into the UK from his home in Montecito, California, to give evidence, also grew tearful as he said the court battle had been a “horrible experience” for his family.

As part of its defence, ANL said Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday journalists provide a “compelling account of a pattern of legitimate sourcing of articles”.

This includes friends and “leaky” social circles, press officers and spokespersons, as well as previous reporting, freelance journalists and stories from other newspapers and news agencies.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Associated Newspapers later hailed the judgment as “an overwhelming victory” and “a magnificent vindication of the Daily Mail’s journalism”.

Editor-in-Chief Paul Dacre also said the “trumped-up” case was a “sinister bid” to impose statutory regulations on the Press.

News.title: Man in his 30s dies & driver injured after lorry with crane attached overturns and hits van – as A-road closed
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FATAL CRASH Man in his 30s dies & driver injured after lorry with crane attached overturns and hits van – as A-road closed

A MAN has tragically died and a driver has been rushed to hospital after a crane-carrying lorry overturned and crashed into a van.

The A37 remains closed while cops continue their investigation into the horror smash in Ston Easton, Somerset, yesterday afternoon.

Emergency crews were scrambled to the collision on the busy A-road shortly after 2.25pm.

The lorry, which had a crane attached, overturned before smashing into the van, Avon and Somerset Police said.





The force confirmed a passenger in the van was tragically declared dead at the scene.

His heartbroken family are currently being supported by specially-trained officers.

Medical teams rushed the van driver to hospital, where he is still being treated for injuries not believed to be life-threatening.

It is understood the lorry driver did not sustain injuries during the horror.



The A37 High Street was completely shut last night as detectives combed the crash site.

And cops confirmed the road is likely to remain shut for “some time” for repairs to the highway.

Avon and Somerset Police urged anyone with information on the collision to get in touch.

Issuing a statement, it said: “A man in his thirties has died following a two-vehicle collision on the A37 at Ston Easton yesterday.



“A lorry, with a crane attached, overturned at about 2.25pm and collided with a van.

“Sadly, a passenger within the van has died at the scene. His family have been informed and they are being supported by a specially-trained officer.

“The van driver has attended hospital with injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening.

“The lorry driver is not believed to have sustained any physical injury.

“Witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage that may assist our enquiries, is asked to contact us quoting reference number 5226235326.”

News.title: Terrifying moment bull rams moving car & smashes through window with horns as beast gets trapped inside with passengers
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a raging bull rams into a moving car and smashes through the window with its horns.

Dramatic footage shows the beast galloping at the car before crashing through the backseat window, leaving the three passengers inside terrified.



The violent attack took place during the patron saint festivities in Iriépal to honour San Roque, a revered Christian saint in Guadalajara, Spain.

Dramatic footage showed the bull running alongside the motor before suddenly running directly at the vehicle.



The animal was likely startled by the car approaching next to it as it launched the aggressive attack.

A powerful blow saw the bull ram into the car with shattered glass sent flying as it cracked the window.

Its horns were just inches away from one of the passengers in the back seat and even closer to the man sitting in the front.

The bull became stuck in the car by its huge horns as the driver tried to speed away out of danger.

Unable to dislodge itself from the smashed up door, the bull was left running alongside the car.

After a few horrifying seconds, the bull managed to get loose but was flung backwards.



The person filming from the back seat caught the bull falling over, appearing to land heavily on its neck.

It comes after a huge bull crashed into a barber shop and charged towards panicking staff in May.

The 1.5-tonne raging bull reportedly slipped the custody of its owner who was planning to slaughter it before the beast escaped and started on the rampage.



In another horror incident, a bull charged at a woman, 55, in the Segovian municipality of Cantalejo.

The bull had escaped from a running of the bulls event in the area earlier this month.

The attack happened when it escaped a barrier and rammed into the woman, causing her to fall backwards and hit her head.

News.title: Faulty oxygen masks and ‘rotting’ axles…furious ex Boeing staff reveal terrifying ‘red flags’ before crashes killed 346
News.content:
DESIGN FOR DISASTER Faulty oxygen masks and ‘rotting’ axles…furious ex Boeing staff reveal terrifying ‘red flags’ before crashes killed 346

WHEN two Boeing aircraft dropped out of the sky within five months of each other, claiming 346 lives, it sparked a major global investigation.

While families grieved and demanded justice for their loved ones, several Boeing workers felt convinced the tragedies were no coincidence.



They claim they had been flagging safety concerns within the company for years, but had been silenced for the fear of losing their jobs.

Accusing senior management of putting profits above passenger safety heartbroken workers turned whistleblowers and joined forces with the bereaved families in a bid to hold the company accountable.



And following the suicide of the first whistleblower John Barnett, more former employers have shared their damning revelations for a Netflix documentary, Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing.

But despite claims of corporate shortcuts, Boeing has escaped any criminal prosecution, leaving the bereaved families still calling for justice.



Some lost loved ones on the Lion Air Flight 610, which went down in October 2018, killing all 189 people on board, and others on the Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, which crashed in March 2019.

Naoise Connolly Ryan, whose husband Mike died on one of the stricken aircrafts, says: “I don’t think I can walk away and just say there is nothing we can do and put my hands in the air.



“There has been no justice, no accountability. It makes me so angry and I think that we have to keep fighting. It can’t be allowed to just stay this way, something has to change.”

Based in Seattle, Boeing was one of the world’s leading aircraft manufacturers, with quality and safety its key watch words.

Aerospace journalist Dominic Gates says things changed in 2005 with the appointment of CEO James McNerney.



He had been a protégé of influential CEO Jack Welch who journalist Dominic Gates says was one of the first in America to focus on maximising profits at all costs.

McNerney was tasked with developing a new airplane – the 787 Dreamliner which was going to cost approx $10 billion to design and build.

Dominic Gates says he received leaked documents showing that Boeing’s plan was to build the plane for $5bn, half of what it would normally have cost.



Boeing outsourced major sections of the plane with parts coming from Italy, Canada, Japan, South Korea, and Australia.

Boeing quality inspector Sam Mohawk says: “You automatically knew that was going to have a direct effect on safety and quality.”

Parts started arriving from the different suppliers, and Dominic Gates says the plan was that the plane would be snapped together in three days.

Gates says when delays started to mount, Boeing planned to build a second 787 production line in an effort to increase production.

The new plant was in South Carolina and experienced staff were sent from Seattle – including quality manager John Barnett.



In a voice recording made in 2020, John Barnett explains: “Part of the agreement that Boeing made with South Carolina was they would hire the majority of employees locally.

“We were doing job fairs, we were hiring people straight out of college. Pretty much we got to if you knew what a screw driver was you were hired for Boeing.”

“These people weren’t trained the way they should.”



And mistakes started to pile up almost immediately.

On one occasion another former Boeing employee claims in the documentary he was walking through the production line and saw a manager using a sledgehammer to pound a pin into a landing gear.

He claims he reported it but no action was taken.

After the launch of the Dreamliner in 2011, Boeing was in major financial trouble. It was facing competition from rival Airbus who announced it was putting new engines on its most popular jet which would save around 20% on fuel costs.

With Airbus over-taking them Jim McNerney wanted a new plane to challenge for top spot but that would take years.



So instead he decided to put new fuel-efficient engines on the existing 737 to create the 737 Max, immediately boosting sales.

McNerney stepped down in 2015 but the cost-cutting agenda would continue under his hand-picked successor Dennis Muilenburg.

John Barnett recalled being called to a Dreamliner where he claimed slivers of metal had been found on electronic wiring under the floor board.

He feared they would cause wires to short circuit and bring down a plane, but when he flagged it up he claimed he was told it would cost too much money and take too much time to clean.

He said: “How much is it going to cost if one of these planes goes down with 350 people on board? I said I will not put my name on this airplane saying it is safe and airworthy but they didn’t want to hear it.”



John Barnett claimed he was then moved from department to department, constantly flagging safety issues, until he eventually felt so worn down he took retirement.

In 2015 alarm bells went off for Boeing quality manager Merle Myers when he claimed some landing axles they had previously scrapped and painted red with the word scrap ended up being used in the Dreamliner production line.

“These parts were basically rotted and as I started to research it I found that scrap parts were put back on the airplane for years and years.”

A corporate investigation was launched – but he claims not one manager was fired.

On March 10 2019 an Ethiopian Airlines plane crashed shortly after take off killing all 157 passengers and crew.



Irish mother Naoise Connolly Ryan, wife of passenger Mick Ryan started to research. “I learned that this wasn’t even the first Max crash. Brand new planes falling from the sky twice. How could this be? I wanted answers.”

A near identical 737 max aircraft had crashed off Indonesia just five months previously, in very similar circumstances.

The Boeing 737 Max fleet was grounded as an investigation was launched, uncovering a chilling catalogue of errors.

Naoise says: “My kids are aware that their dad got on a plane and the plane was made by bad guys. My son asked me, ‘will we catch the bad guys?’ And I said I don’t know, we will have to wait and see.”

Muileburg refused to quit, but was eventually fired.



He was replaced by chairman of the board Dave Calhoun, as Boeing faced multiple investigations, including a criminal one.

But in 2021 it was announced the DoJ would end the criminal investigation, with a probationary period, if Boeing paid a $2.5bn fine and met other conditions.

Furious Naoise Connolly Ryan says: ” The CEO should have been prosecuted, instead they wrote that senior management knew nothing about what was going on.

“It is utter disbelief that somebody could get away with killing 346 people.”

John Barnett knew his safety concerns were still relevant, so he turned whistleblower.



He said: “We are talking aeroplanes, we are talking people’s lives, we are talking flying public, I can’t sit back and let that go. I wasn’t going to sit down and shut up.”

And the families started to keep track of incidents with Boeing’s aircraft and liaise with whistleblowers to build a case.

But the new Boeing CEO told authorities he was putting safety first, and had created a speak-up programme for employees to voice concerns.

And the Boeing 737 Max fleet was allowed to take to the skies once again.

But once the Max was back in the air, staff say the whole atmosphere at Boeing changed.



Quality inspectors including Sam Mohawk and Merle Myers say they reported critical issues via the new speak-up programme, but say they suffered intimidation at work and feared for their jobs for speaking out.

Meanwhile John Barnett filed a case against Boeing for exposure to a hostile work environment.

One of the issues John claimed he was told to drop was his discovery that some of the oxygen masks on board the aircraft did not work, potentially putting lives at risk.

Two days before the expiry date for Boeing’s probationary period, John’s worst nightmare came true. Alaska Flight 1282 declared an emergency.

A door plug panel had blown out of the aircraft, the cabin began to depressurise and oxygen masks dropped down – but some passengers said theirs did not work and filed law suits.



Thankfully the plane landed safely – but it was a Boeing 737 Max.

An investigation revealed that workers inside the Boeing factory had taken off the door plug to fix things that suppliers had got wrong.

To do so they would have had to remove four retaining bolts – and a photo revealed that some of the bolts had never been put back.

Naiose Connolly Ryan says: “Everything that we had been saying, the Boeing culture is broken and that these defective planes are continuing to fly had just been proved correct.

“In a way it is a miracle, because not only was no-one killed.”



As the investigation was underway, John Barnett’s case against Boeing was being heard in court.

In March 2024, after seven hours of gruelling questioning by Boeing’s counsel, John returned to his hotel room.

He was found dead in his truck outside the next day with self-inflicted gunshot wound to his head.

John had tragically left a suicide note inside his Boeing notebook which said: “F**k Boeing. I can’t do this any longer. Enough. Family and friends I loved you all.”

His lawyer Rob Turkewitz says: “One thing is for sure, Boeing may not have pulled the trigger, but Boeing is responsible for John’s death.”



Furious at his friend’s death and how he had been treated by Boeing management, Merle Myers also turned whistleblower went to the New York Times with his claims about Boeing’s safety failures.

And other employees followed suit.

In June 2024, Boeing’s CEO Dave Calhoun was brought before a government hearing to answer claims that the company put profits over people.

But in November last year the Department of Justice dropped its criminal case against the company for the 737 Max crashes. Boeing was required to pay $1.1bn fine and commit to improving safety, quality and compliance. No Boeing CEO has ever been charged.

The last four Boeing CEOs received compensation and retirement benefits totalling almost $500 million.



As of March 2026, Boeing’s commercial airline division has not turned a profit since 2018, losing an estimated $40bn over that period.

In August last year, Boeing settled John Barnett’s lawsuit for an undisclosed amount. A second lawsuit for unlawful death remains pending.

The Sun has approached Boeing for a response who said: “The allegations in this film have been widely reported over the years.

“Some remain unfounded claims to this day while others are issues that Boeing thoroughly addressed or continues to improve upon under the rigorous oversight of our regulators.

“Today, we are grateful that customers, industry experts, policymakers, and our employees are seeing improvements in how we work together and deliver quality products. Our team is working every day to meet our commitments and earn the trust of those who depend on us.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing is on Netflix now to www.netflix.com/freefallareckoningforboeing.

News.title: Moment man nearly runs over woman before falling off motorcycle & sprinting away from cops before running out of breath
News.content:
THIS is the moment a man nearly runs over a woman before falling off his motorcycle and sprinting away from cops.

Shocking footage shows the man racing through the streets of Oldham, Greater Manchester, earlier this week with cops in close pursuit.



Greater Manchester Police posted the clip to social media alongside the caption: “A game of cat and mouse that ended with the mouse calling it quits…”

It begins with the man attempting to flee from officers on a motorbike, flying down the street past a long line of motors.



He then sharply turns, cutting across both lanes and almost hitting a woman and missing her by inches as she crosses the road.

Remarkably, as the suspect approaches an oncoming field, he launches himself from the bike, letting it veer off and crash on the grass nearby.



After hitting the ground himself, the man then sprints away as the officer continues to pursue him.

Running out of breath, the man then gives up and throws his helmet to the floor in defeat.

Greater Manchester Police confirmed the man was arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving, failing to stop and driving without insurance.

The man was put in cuffs on August 19 and will attend court later this year, they added.

The force said the latest incident was part of a crack down on the anti-social and dangerous use of off-road bikes, e-bikes and quad bikes, called Operation Hurricane.



This month alone, cops have made six arrests, four of which where for drug driving, and seized 14 vehicles.

Police Sergeant Tom Layton from Oldham Neighbourhood Team said: “These vehicles can be extremely dangerous when used irresponsibly.

“They are often ridden in places where people simply do not expect to encounter a motorbike or quad bike, creating obvious risks for pedestrians, cyclists and other road users.

“A split-second decision can have serious consequences.”

He added: “We are grateful for the support we receive from residents.



“The information they provide helps us build a clearer picture of what’s happening in their communities and allows us to target our activity where it can make the biggest difference.”

Anyone with information about the anti-social use of bikes is encouraged to contact the police.

News.title: Female bar worker sexually assaulted at seaside town centre nightclub as cops release CCTV in hunt for man
News.content:

ATTACK PROBE Female bar worker sexually assaulted at seaside town centre nightclub as cops release CCTV in hunt for man

A FEMALE bar worker has allegedly been sexually assaulted in a popular nightclub – as cops release CCTV in the hunt for her attacker.

The victim was reportedly targeted in the early hours while working at the Camel Bar in Bournemouth, Dorset.



She was allegedly attacked at the popular club on Old Christchurch Road at around 5am.

The man is said to have initially grabbed the woman’s arm multiple times during the horror attack on July 19.



He then touched her inappropriately over her clothing, according to Dorset Police.

The force quickly launched an investigation into the alleged sexual assault.



Officers have since released CCTV of a man they wish to identify in connection with the horror.

PC Bethany Dyson, of Bournemouth Police, said: “I am now in a position to issue an image of a man I would like to identify.

“If you recognise him or have information about his identity, please get in touch.”

Issuing a statement, Dorset Police repeated the plea and urged anyone with information to contact the force.



It read: “Officers are issuing an image of a man they would like to identify after a woman was inappropriately touched in Bournemouth.

“At around 5am on Sunday 19 July 2026, a man grabbed a female member of staff’s arm multiple times in Camel Bar in Old Christchurch Road before touching her inappropriately over her clothing.

“Anyone with information is asked to contact Dorset Police online or by calling 101, quoting occurrence number 55260110464.

“Alternatively, Crimestoppers can be contacted anonymously online using its website or by calling Freephone 0800 555 111.”

News.title: EMB: MIDNIGHT >> Prostate cancer becomes most common cancer in Britain after drive to get men checked
News.content:
EMB: MIDNIGHT >> Prostate cancer becomes most common cancer in Britain after drive to get men checked

Prostate cancer is now the most common cancer in the UK according to Macmillan Cancer Support after Olympic legend Sir Chris Hoy encouraged more men to get NHS check

View 5 Images More men are getting a prostate cancer diagnosis

Prostate has become the most common cancer in the UK.

‌



Macmillan Cancer Support has said the number of men living with prostate cancer in the UK has surged by 100,000 since 2020.

‌



Analysis by the charity shows 68,000 men are newly diagnosed in the UK each year - the equivalent of one diagnosis every eight minutes. This compares to 59,000 new breast cancer diagnoses annually. It comes after a campaign by Olympic legend Sir Chris Hoy, who has a terminal diagnosis, supported by charities and a host of politicians calling for more men to get routine checks.

‌



Macmillan’s latest estimates show there are now around 600,000 men living with prostate cancer in the UK, compared with around 500,000 in 2020. It says it means prostate cancer is now the most common type of cancer diagnosed in the UK.

View 5 Images Sir Chris Hoy is calling for men with a family history of prostate cancer to be invited for an NHS test

NHS prostate cancer checks REJECTED for at-risk men despite calls from legends like Sir Chris Hoy READ MORE :

The charity has warned that "myths" surrounding the disease could be preventing men from getting checked.

‌



View 5 Images Currently over-50s can request an NHS check (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Dr Anthony Cunliffe, lead medical adviser at Macmillan Cancer Support, said: "One of the biggest misunderstandings I hear is that feeling well means you cannot have prostate cancer.

"Many people are surprised to learn that, in reality, prostate cancer often develops without symptoms in its early stages, which is why it's important to have a conversation with your GP if you're worried."

‌



Previous data collated by Cancer Research UK indicated there were 58,000 new prostate cancer diagnoses each year, compared to 59,000 for breast cancer. The Macmillan analysis suggests the most common cancer in men has overtaken the most common cancer in women.

View 5 Images Some prostate cancer tumours can be slow growing enough to be harmless (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The charity said some men with prostate cancer will not see symptoms for many years and symptoms usually occur when the cancer is large enough to press on the urethra - the tube which passes urine.

‌



When symptoms occur they include: difficulty urinating; needing to urinate more often than usual, especially at night; a feeling that the bladder has not been completely emptied; an urgency when needing the toilet; blood in urine; blood in semen.

Macmillan said it is important for men to speak to their GP if they have any of these symptoms. Dr Cunliffe added: "Prostate cancer generally occurs in men over 50 but it can develop earlier in some groups, including black men and men with a family history of prostate cancer."

View 5 Images Sir Chris in his cycling heyday (Image: PA)

‌



Consultant surgeon Ben Lamb, lecturer at the Barts Cancer Institute, said: “The recent growth in the number of men living with the disease is more likely to be driven principally by increased and earlier diagnosis combined with better survival.

“This is not simply a story of ‘more cancer’. It is a story of a growing population of men who may live for many years with the consequences of diagnosis and treatment.”

Dr Alastair Lamb, clinical reader at St Bartholomew's Hospital, said: "There's no evidence whatsoever that prostate cancer is on the increase. Whenever prostate cancer incidence rises it's always due to diagnostic practice rather than increased in underlying presence of disease... the fact that death rates are static confirm that there is no increase in disease."

‌



Sir Chris Hoy sparked a national debate as to whether men with no symptoms should be offered the PSA test. The six-time Olympic champion is calling for more men to be proactively offered tests and at an earlier age. Currently men over 50 can ask for a PSA test from their NHS GP. If levels are raised they will receive further tests and scans.

But earlier this year the UK National Screening Committee recommended against screening all men using the blood test, saying it is "likely to cause more harm than good".

The UKNSC used population modelling and concluded current blood tests are not reliable enough and likely to over-treat men for too many benign tumours which would have never caused them harm.

Article continues below

Prostate cancer can grow very slowly in some men. Current screening methods struggle to separate out fast growing disease from harmless tumours.

News.title: Victim of Manchester Arena terror attack felt 'forgotten' after nine months in hospital
News.content:
Victim of Manchester Arena terror attack felt 'forgotten' after nine months in hospital

Paul Price was waiting for his 13-year-old daughter to leave the Ariana Grande concert in 2017 when suicide bomber Salman Abedi detonated an improvised explosive device, killing 22

Manchester terror attack survivor was not offered enough support

A victim of the Manchester Arena terror attack has told how he thought “my life is over” after he was discharged from hospital.

‌



Paul Price was waiting outside for his 13-year-old daughter to leave the Ariana Grande concert in 2017 when suicide bomber Salman Abedi detonated an improvised explosive device, killing 22 innocent people.

‌



Paul lost his partner, Detective Constable Elaine McIver, in the blast and suffered life-changing injuries which saw him spend nine months in hospital.

‌



View 2 Images Elaine McIver tragically died in Manchester Arena attack (Image: Arena Inquiry)

Speaking on the first dedicated national memorial day for victims of terror, Paul told how he felt forgotten after his lengthy spell in rehab. He said: “As you can imagine, after something like this, losing the love of my life, losing the person I was, losing the career I had, I came out of hospital nine months later totally lost, directionless and I thought life was over for me.

“All the time I was in hospital I was told ‘don’t worry Paul, you’ll be looked after when you get out, there will be loads of support, loads of help, just concentrate on your rehab’, and that’s what I did. I came out of hospital nine months later to nothing.”

‌



He told the BBC: “I remember saying to myself ‘Paul you’ve been in hospital too long and they’ve forgotten about you’, and they had. I couldn’t live on my own at the time, I was living with my parents who were in no position really to look after me.

“I went from a fully equipped rehab ward to my parents house with a physio coming out once a week to look for things in the house to aid in my recovery. There was no-one knocking on my door saying ‘right, this has happened to you Paul, that life is over now, but you’ve still got a life’.

“As far as I was concerned my life was over and I needed help. I was navigating so many things, life changing injuries, the loss of Elaine. I wasn’t in a position to start creating a new life for myself. I was left alone for such a long time.”

‌



View 2 Images Police at scene of Manchester Arena attack (Image: PA)

Paul is also quoted in a report which claims survivors of terror attacks are still being ‘mistreated and neglected’.

The campaign group Survivors Against Terror (SAT) claims financial support for victims is fragmented and can depend on individual circumstances such as employment and pension arrangements

‌



In the report, Paul said: “The blast changed my life forever. I suffered catastrophic injuries that left me unable to return to work after a lifetime of employment. Alongside my own injuries and the months of hospital treatment and rehabilitation that followed, I had to face the devastating loss of Elaine.

“I turned to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority believing it would provide recognition and support as I tried to rebuild my life. Instead, the process became another source of trauma."

He highlighted being repeatedly required to revisit the events of that night and provide extensive evidence to prove the impact of what happened.

Article continues below

He added: “The delays, uncertainty and constant need to justify my injuries left me feeling as though I was not being supported, but questioned.

“After surviving a terrorist attack and losing Elaine, the last thing I expected was to feel as though I had to prove my suffering to a system that was supposed to recognise it.”

News.title: Young children and pregnant women told to avoid runny eggs over salmonella risk
News.content:
Young children and pregnant women told to avoid runny eggs over salmonella risk

The warning also includes anything that might include uncooked eggs, such as mayonnaise, souffle or hollandaise sauce

View Image Multiple groups of people have been warned, including pregnant women (Image: Getty)

Toddlers, the elderly and pregnant women have been warned not to eat under-cooked eggs in restaurants amid a salmonella outbreak.

‌



The warning also includes anything that might include uncooked eggs, such as mayonnaise, souffle or hollandaise sauce. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) said, however, that well-cooked eggs in eateries are fine to eat.

‌



One person has died and more than 200 others were left ill during the outbreak, which could be linked to eggs imported to the UK. Between August 11 last year and August 1 this year, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said 207 cases were confirmed in the country, with 199 of these in England.

‌



Almost 40 per cent of those were admitted to hospital, while two people developed potentially life-threatening bloodstream infections. The ages of those who became ill range from babies to people in their 90s.

Health officials said they are investigating whether the outbreak could be connected to eggs imported from outside the UK. Salmonella is a family of bacteria that can live in the digestive tracts of animals, including chickens, which is why eggs and poultry are among the foods commonly associated with the infection.

Article continues below

FSA chief scientific adviser Ian Young told the BBC that the young, elderly, pregnant and vulnerable should particularly be cautious of eating eggs when out, making sure that they have been "very well cooked". He said: "If people are eating out or consuming eggs or egg-containing products from cafes and restaurants then for those people in particular who are young, elderly, pregnant or vulnerable, it's important to make sure that any eggs or egg products that you consume in those settings have been very well cooked."

Mr Young explained that it is safe for people to buy British eggs from supermarkets thanks to chickens bred here being vaccinated against common salmonella strains. Speaking to the Mirror, Steve Horner, a kitchen hygiene expert from Cladding Monkey, explained: "No link has been identified to British eggs or poultry, as hens in the UK are vaccinated against salmonella."

Mr Young also described the current outbreak as "unusually large and rapidly increasing", warning people to "be careful".

News.title: Premier League price of pints and pies soars by up to 27% at football grounds
News.content:
Premier League price of pints and pies soars by up to 27% at football grounds

Fans face paying up to £7.50 for a beer and £6.50 for a pie while attending matches this season

View 4 Images Football fans are facing paying more than ever for beers and pies at Premier League stadiums (Image: PA Archive/Press Association Images)

Premier League football fans face paying up to £7.99-a pint inside stadiums this season, as clubs are accused of having “no regard” for their most loyal supporters.

‌



Bournemouth fans face the biggest price hike as the Cherries have upped their prices by £1.50 to £7-a-pint (27%) at the Vitality Stadium. Leeds fans face a 23% increase as the club have raised lager prices to £6.75-a-pint at Elland Road this season - a £1.25 increase. And Manchester United have increased pint prices at Old Trafford by 16% to £6.60.

‌



In total, 13 of the 20 Premier League clubs have upped their lager prices this season, with the average price of a pint at top flight grounds now £6.25 - a 33p rise on last season. Prices of pies are also rising by up to an inflation-busting 27% this season.

‌



View 4 Images Fans of Chelsea face paying £7.99-a-pint inside Stamford Bridge this season (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Mo Salah's heartwarming reunion with biggest fan Isaac after leaving Liverpool READ MORE :

Consumer expert Scott Dixon, said: “Having a few beers and a pie with friends at a football match is pretty much part of a ritual. Add in the soaring cost of replica shirts and season tickets, and fans will rightly feel they are being ripped off.

“The cost-of-living crisis is used to justify rip-off prices everywhere and it’s wearing thin with consumers now. Clubs charge what they think they can get away across the board with no regard for loyal fans.”

‌



Chelsea fans will have to fork out the most if they want a pint during a match, with prices up £1.14 to a whopping £7.99-a-pint at Stamford Bridge. Fulham fans face the second highest price, with the prospect of paying £7.50 for a pint of lager at Craven Cottage, despite the west London club freezing prices this season.

Champions Arsenal, who will kick-off the 26/27 season in the curtain-raising opener against Coventry tonight, are third in the lager league. The Gunners are the only club to drop prices, taking 20p off the cost of a pint, but their beers will still cost £7. Liverpool have the cheapest lager in the league, with fans at Anfield able to buy a pint for £4.80.

View 4 Images Bournemouth fans face the biggest price hike as the Cherries have upped their prices by £1.50 to £7-a-pint (Image: PA)

‌



Meanwhile, sixteen clubs have increased pie prices, with the average cost now £5.84 - a 25p rise compared to last season. The largest pie increases are found at Crystal Palace, where prices have shot up 27% on last season. Fans will have to fork out £6.50 for a pie at home games - compared to £5.10 last season.

Arsenal top the table for the most expensive pie. Supporters there will pay £6.95, the most expensive in the Premier League, despite dropping their prices by £1.90. Fans paid £8.85 last season, with the new prices representing a 21% cut.

Fulham have also dropped their pie prices by 50p to £6. The least expensive pie is again at Anfield, with Liverpool charging their fans £4.50.

‌



We contacted every Premier League to ask them for their prices this season. Some said that while their beer costs have increased, they are offering early bird discounts and bundle offers on food and drinks.

View 4 Images Crystal Palace have increased the price of their pies to £6.50, up from £5.10 last season (Image: PA)

For Everton’s first three home Premier League fixtures - against Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Ipswich Town -the Toffees have a pre-game early bird price of £4.50 a pint. The club are also donating 50p from every qualifying pint sold to a flag and banner fund set up by the 1878s fan group.
