News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

Sports.title: Essential last-minute cheat sheet for Dream Team bosses ahead of Gameweek 1 deadline
Sports.content:
THE deadline for Gameweek 1 is at 8pm today!

Whether you’ve spent the last fortnight tinkering with your Dream Team or have left it until the last minute, we encourage you to read our concise cheat sheet — everything you need to know in just a couple of minutes.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Fixtures, Fixtures, Fixtures

It’s easy to fall into the trap of looking too far into the future when building your initial team.



Generally, it’s a better idea to let the schedule determine your strategy and that means identifying imminent fixtures to target.

On paper, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Leeds have relatively favourable openings this season.

And Sunderland’s first three fixtures catch the eye: Ipswich (a), Fulham (h), Brentford (a).



Additionally, it’s important to note that 11 Premier League clubs – those not involved in Europe – will play twice in Gameweek 1 with Carabao Cup second round fixtures set to take place across Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Rotation is to be expected in the early rounds of the domestic cups but there could be some juicy points of offer from match-ups such as: Chelsea v Luton, Spurs v Charlton and Fulham v AFC Wimbledon.

And it’s not too early to take the European fixtures into equation either as the Champions League will commence in earnest from early September (Gameweek 3).

The best managers milk the schedule for all it is worth and that sometimes means planning three, four or five weeks in advance while remaining flexible and reacting appropriately to the unfolding drama.



Availability Issues

This may sound obvious but we strongly recommend you take the time to check your players are available.

A quick glance at the Stats Centre reveals that more than a few gaffers are backing the likes of William Saliba (£5m), Jurrien Timber (£5m) and Hugo Ekitike (£5m), who are all injured.

While Bruno Guimaraes (£4m), Benjamin Sesko (£4m) and Jeremy Doku (£5m) are among the doubts.

Gameweek 1 is unique in that the deadline falls approximately 75 minutes after the starting line-ups for the first fixture are confirmed.



This will give you time to check your Arsenal/Coventry players but you can’t afford to take risks with the other fixtures — although our Substitute feature provides a helpful safety net.

Play Dream Team this season! £100,000 in prize money up for grabs in 2026/27 Free to enter

Play in Mini Leagues against your mates

£60,000 jackpot for the overall winner

£1,000 prize for winning Gameweek 1

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW!

Build Your Budget

Earning points is the name of the game but smart Dream Team bosses know the importance of building budget throughout the first few months of the season.

Player prices will fluctuate based on performance with changes coming into effect at the start of each Gameweek (from GW2).

You should take this into account when making transfers as savvy swaps will allow you to recruit players before they become more expensive while simultaneously ditching assets before they depreciate.

Work the stock market to your advantage and eventually you’ll see be able to afford several pricey superstars — this is particularly beneficial for juicy Champions League Gameweeks.



Expensive stars such as Erling Haaland (£8.5m) and Bruno Fernandes (£7m) will have to work hard to maintain their lofty prices – though of course they’re capable – while cheaper assets are held to a lower standard.

Knowing when to go all out for points and when to prioritise your budget is a key strategic element of the game.

New Arrivals

This time last year, Florian Wirtz (£5m) was among the most popular players in Dream Team as managers expected the German midfielder to hit the ground running at Liverpool.

As it happened, the former Bayer Leverkusen needed some time to adjust to his new surroundings and provided precious few points before December, by which time his ownership had plummeted.



The lesson being, it’s incredibly difficult to predict how new signings will bed in, even those as talented as Wirtz.

This is not to say you should avoid all new arrivals as, inevitably, some will make an instant impact.

It’s just that selecting too many of these players from the get-go can be risky.

Proven performers usually guarantee a steady start before the season has taken shape.



Have Fun!

Above all, remember that Dream Team is supposed to be entertaining.

If following the advice given above would make reduce your enjoyment then disregard it and play your own game.

Picking a player on pure gut feeling and getting 20 points from them on a Saturday afternoon is greatly satisfying — don’t deny yourself that feeling because a stranger on the internet makes some quip about xG.

Last season’s overall winner banked £60,000 by trusting his instincts and one of his very few mistakes came when he was swayed by other opinions.

The Manchester United goalkeeper is in his second season out on loan at the Turkish club, while Salah has just arrived as a surprise package following his departure from Liverpool.

One of the attractions of Trabzon is that it is a predominantly Muslim city, with lots of mosques and a culture that has similarities with Salah’s native Egypt.



Salah and his family were therefore happy to make the move, with the environment offering a sense of familiarity despite being thousands of miles from home.

Sports.title: SunSport’s referee expert explains nine new rules coming to Premier League – and verdict on three major changes to VAR
Sports.content:
HOWARD WEBB revealed this week he would like to apply a “light touch approach” to VAR.

But this should have been the Prem‘s strategy for the last seven years since it was introduced in the 2019/20 season.



Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Webb and his predecessor Mike Riley have allowed a forensic application which was totally unnecessary and contrasted with the IFAB protocol.

After talks with the 20 Prem clubs, Webb now says refs should reserve it for “those situations which are clear and obviously wrong”.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

So let’s hope – and pray – that we see a big improvement in our use of VAR and refereeing standards in general this term.

Webb has talked the talk for some time and now it’s time for him to deliver.

We lost one of our top refs Anthony Taylor after he hung up his whistle following this summer’s World Cup.

I find it baffling that Taylor is no longer in our system as he was appointed the Turkish Football Federation’s new director of elite refereeing.

It has been clear for some time that we haven’t got many top-quality refs and there is a real lack of depth in the top-flight.

Webb and co have opted to develop and expose more refs to football‘s elite by merging Select Group One and Two.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

While there is a bigger pool of officials – 39 in total – in the new Professional Referee Group officials, many of them have never refereed a Prem game.

Another point to note is this merger will make it easier for bosses to move the officials between the Prem and Championship without fanfare.

Arsenal‘s clash with Coventry at the Emirates tonight kicks-off the new season and nine new laws are set to be implemented.

I like the five-second countdowns for throw-ins and goal kicks as we saw in the World Cup.

It will speed up the game but we need to be consistent in our application.

Players who go down will have to leave the pitch for a minute.



This will not apply if they have been fouled and the offending player has been cautioned for the offence.

For the “goalkeeper timeout,” where a stopper is seen by a physio, the manager will have ten seconds to nominate an outfield player who must leave the pitch for 60 seconds. This will not come into play if the goalkeeper has been fouled or is bleeding.

Substituted players have 10 seconds to trudge off the pitch and if they don’t, the sub will have to wait a minute. It’s another positive change because we don’t want to see time-wasting in our game.



Ref chiefs have clarified that any kick of the ball during a goal-kick routine will be treated as the goalkeeper having taken it.

On the VAR front, they can now review second yellow cards. This will only apply to ones that actually have been handed out and NOT potential second cautions that did not come to pass.

Set-piece goals can also be reviewed if a foul occurred before the kick was taken. If this is the case, the goal will be chalked off and the set-piece retaken.

VAR can also correct acts of mistaken identity by the on-field referee. For example, if a player has been booked, but the offence was actually committed by another player, VAR will intervene to see the right player penalised. This rule will only be applied to the same infringement.

Direct officials’ wording from Premier League Match Centre

Halsey Verdict: Good decision



“Everyone wants feedback from the officials and this is a good move for them to explain their decisions. The fans are just as important as the players and managers. While we won’t hear from them directly and their quotes will be in a written form, it is a step in the right direction.”

In-game audio from the Ref Cam

Halsey Verdict: Bad decision

“This is fine in theory but I doubt we will get a true reflection of what goes on during a game. Shop floor language is used and that’s how officials manage the players. I fear we will only hear what Pro Refs want us to hear in a watered down version. Players will also worry about speaking to officials because it may get aired.”

Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel

Halsey Verdict: Good decision

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is a positive change as everyone should be able to view the results of the KMI panel. The five panel members have met since the 2022-23 season but their findings have officially remained private.



“I do hope we get full transparency and find out who is on the panel.”

Sports.content:
The latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and around the world as deadline day edges closer

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog on Friday, August 20.

The big news on Thursday was that Liverpool had a £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton & Hove Albion. The Reds have been scouring the market for wingers this summer and tabled an opening offer for the Gambia international after shortlisting him earlier this year.

However, while the player is believed to be keen on a move to Anfield, Liverpool’s offer falls short of Brighton’s valuation, and it remains to be seen whether the Reds will return with another offer.

Curtis Jones, meanwhile, is set to complete a move to Inter Milan in a transfer that could be worth £30million. He has had permission to fly to Italy to undergo a medical after a deal was agreed on Thursday.

While Manchester City are pursuing a deal for Palmeiras winger Allan, as Savinho remains in talks with Tottenham Hotspur. But one man who won’t be leaving his club this summer is Myles Lewis-Skelly, as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta yesterday ruled out a transfer happening this summer.

The Gunners also continue to be linked with a move for Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, with one report claiming a deal between the Spanish club and the Gunners had been agreed. Alvarez, though, still favours a move to Barcelona.

And Manchester United have reportedly contacted Barcelona to ask about Alejandro Balde's situation at the club. The Red Devils are keen to add a left-back to the squad this summer, and it is claimed that Barca are willing to listen to offers for Balde this summer.

We will keep you up to date on those moves and much more right here on our blog below...

Sports.title: Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed
Sports.content:
Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed

Reigning champions Arsenal get their Premier League season underway tonight against Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium - but Mikel Arteta has a new fitness doubt

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Frank Lampard go head-to-head this evening as Arsenal host Coventry (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Mikel Arteta is sweating on the fitness of Bruno Guimaraes heading into tonight’s game against Coventry City. Arsenal begin the defence of their Premier League title against Frank Lampard’s side at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Guimaraes, who joined the Gunners from Newcastle United earlier this month, was forced off during the Community Shield victory over Manchester City last weekend. And speaking on Thursday afternoon, Arteta admitted: "Let's see how it is, it's evolving well, but let's see for tomorrow."

‌



However, Arteta will be without defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber. Saliba is continuing his rehabilitation from a back injury sustained at the World Cup, while Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

‌



“No, I said in the next few weeks,” Arteta said on Thursday when asked if Timber can join team training this week. “He's not training with the group yet.”

But there was better news for Gunners supporters, with Arteta confirming that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are fit to start against the Sky Blues. The Arsenal boss said: “Yes, they're ready to be involved, yes.”

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas READ MORE :

While Frank Lampard confirmed on Thursday that Coventry will be without striker Haji Wright for the games against the Gunners. Wright was Coventry’s top scorer last season, scoring 17 times as his side won the Sky Bet Championship.

‌



The striker has been absent from recent friendly matches against RCD Espanyol and AS Monaco. And Lampard admitted his star man could be out for as long as 12 weeks. He said: “Haji Wright won’t be available for the Arsenal game.

“He won’t be available for a little while, he’s got a very serious quad injury which is disappointing for Haji and for us. It’s certainly going to be a number of weeks, could even be up to 12 weeks.”

Lampard, though, did confirm that both Ephron Mason-Clark and Jack Rudoni will be in contention to feature at the Emirates after they missed games in pre-season.

‌



View 2 Images Haji Wright won't be available for Coventry City (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Coventry boss also admitted his side need to be ready for “tougher times” this season ahead of their Premier League curtain-raiser. He said: “We will go through tougher times this year for sure because of the competition we’re up against now so we’ll need resilience in moments calmness in moments.

‌



“An important part of my role is to have that balance and through having a long playing career through having a managerial career where I’ve had some really great moments and some difficult moments.

“But as a club we will need to stick together in those moments but I want to sound like I’m being too negative before something’s happened. It’s just a reality that we need to be ready for.

“Second spell at Chelsea wasn’t great for me, for a PR point. But having been through the challenges for good and for bad in my managerial career I think it puts me in a better spot to deal with – don’t get too high, don’t get too low – continue and focus on your.”

Sports.title: Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark
Sports.content:
Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark

Tottenham have spent heavily so far this summer following a dismal campaign and Roberto De Zerbi’s men are now set to raid Manchester City for two big-money signings

View 2 Images Spurs have agreed a deal to sign Savinho (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham have agreed a deal worth up to £85m to sign Manchester City winger Savinho. The North London side are long-term admirers of the Brazilian winger, having failed to agree terms on a €50million (£43.3m) deal last summer.

‌



But they have retained their interest in the 22-year-old and are now close to finally securing his services. According to The Athletic, Spurs have agreed to pay £75m up-front for the former Troyes man, with £10m in potential bonuses.

‌



Should the deal go through as expected, it would represent a record sale for City, eclipsing the £81m sale of Julian Alvarez to Atletico Madrid in 2024.

‌



Savinho would also become the latest high-profile departure from the Etihad Stadium this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Nathan Ake, Bernardo Silva and John Stones having all left alongside former boss Pep Guardiola.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sales might not even be finished there, either. Spurs are also in talks with City over a deal for Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush.

‌



A deal for both him and Savinho is expected to cost around £140m - meaning Marmoush is valued at around £55m. The 27-year-old only joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt in January last year and has gone on to net 16 goals in 62 appearances.

Meanwhile, Savinho joined the club from French side Troyes in 2024 but has only netted twice in 53 Premier League outings.

Once their moves to North London are complete, they will become the latest arrivals in what has been an astonishing £369m rebuild under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs have already signed Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke for big fees, while Marcos Senesi, Andrew Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all joined on free transfers.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Marmoush is expected to follow Savinho to North London (Image: Getty Images)

Spurs start their season against London rivals Brentford on Saturday evening, while Man City entertain Bournemouth on Sunday. Ahead of that game, City boss Enzo Maresca has already hinted that more signings could arrive before the deadline.

He said: "We knew already before the game the things that we need to do. It is not because we lost the game. We are quite clear. For sure, we are going to do something before the transfer window closes."

Article continues below

City have been linked with Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi but the Italian remained tight-lipped on a deal. He added: "He is still a Lille player. But any new signing as soon as they arrive, it’s better [for us], because we have the Premier League starting in one week."

Sports.title: Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas
Sports.content:
Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas

Arsenal will kick off their Premier League title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday night and a few new signings could potentially be in line to appear for the Gunners

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to guide Arsenal to a second, consecutive title (Image: Getty Images)

For the first time in over 20 years, Arsenal head into a Premier League season as defending champions. The North London side waltzed to their fourth title under the stewardship of Mikel Arteta last term, finally getting over the line after years of near misses.

‌



And while the celebrations of them hoisting the trophy at Selhurst Park back in May will be fresh in the minds of every player and fan, it’s now back down to business.

‌



Arsenal kick off the defence of their title on Friday night as they welcome newly-promoted Coventry City to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Supporters have already managed to get a glimpse of the champions as they eased past Manchester City to win the Community Shield. New signings Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes were handed their debuts but did either of the pair do enough to start in Arsenal’s league opener?

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Before we answer that question, let’s start in defence where Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has a pretty simple task ahead of him. Last season’s Golden Glove winner David Raya will of course start between the sticks - and the defence in front of him effectively picks itself.

‌



Both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber are ruled out through injury, which opens the door to Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White. Brazilian centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes will partner the former in the heart of defence.

There’s then a debate to be had at the other fullback spot, where Riccardo Calafiori, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Piero Hincapie could all play. But given the Italian’s performance in the Community Shield, Arteta may just stick with what he already has.

Academy graduate Lewis-Skelly shone in Cardiff against City, so it feels very harsh to suggest that he could drop out. But Declan Rice is now fit and ready to go, Arteta did express some fitness doubts about new signing Bruno Guimaraes - but that's nothing new for the Gunners boss, he should still start.

‌



View 2 Images Declan Rice might start against Coventry (Image: Getty Images)

It’s also very difficult to envisage Arteta not starting captain Martin Odegaard for the Gunners’ Premier League opener.

When it comes to his attack, the Arsenal boss now has a wealth of options to choose from. Summer arrival Tzolis enjoyed a bright start to life with his new club in the Community Shield after notching two assists and that performance might well have been enough to earn a starting spot against Coventry.

‌



Noni Madueke started on the opposite flank against City, but Arteta might be tempted to draft in Bukayo Saka for a start.

There is then another debate to be had in the central attacking position, where Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus are all options. The German scored against City - and appeared to have usurped Gyokeres in the pecking order at the end of last season - so is probably a good bet to start again.

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry: Raya; Calafiori, Gabriel, Mosquera, White; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Tzolis, Saka, Havertz.

Sports.title: 'Keep on running!' Fury claims AJ fight in doubt
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has claimed his fight against Anthony Joshua is now in serious doubt after his British heavyweight rival asked for 'more money'.

Fury and Joshua have been holding talks about staging their long-awaited fight in November, with Madison Square Garden in New York emerging as the likely location.

But Fury has suggested in a social media video the blockbuster bout could fall through due to Joshua's request for a bigger fight purse.

Sky Sports understands Joshua has signed a contract for the fight and Matchroom are still working towards an announcement.

"Quick update for you. It doesn't look like they are going to sign the fight and it doesn't look like it is going to happen all because [Joshua's promoter] Eddie Hearn and that want more money," Fury said.

"They have already had that much money off Turki (Alalshikh) over the last few years Eddie and AJ, they have had boxing deals, they have had darts deals, they have had snooker deals, they have had everything.

"And yet, they have got the audacity and cheek of flea-bitten rats to ask for more money from old Turki that you have had combined over the last couple of years.

"Keep on running you cowards."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Joe Gallagher is backing the potential Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury fight to take place at Madison Square Garden

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has confirmed the original fight contract stipulated that the bout would be staged in the UK.

Matchroom Boxing CEO Frank Smith had told Sky Sports earlier this week it was a 'critical week' for negotiations but he was optimistic about an agreement.

"It will be disappointing for it not to be in the UK, but at the same time if it means seeing the fight, we all want to see that fight happen," said Smith. "Let's see how things play out.

"We're following the terms of what we signed up to right now, which is a fight in the UK. That is what we signed up to and when the fight was announced in March, April time, the fight was signed, those were the terms we signed up for.

"They are the conversations really that are taking place right now. MSG is a proposed venue that they would like to look at, i.e The Ring Magazine, Saudi delegation, so let's see.

"I think November is possible. Later in November is possible, but again the next seven to 10 days, a lot of progress has got to be made in order to make that happen to get [fighters] into camp to give yourself that eight-to-10-week period, a dedicated camp away from all the promotional obligations."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury's manager Spencer Brown admits he is concerned about the delay in announcing the fight against Anthony Joshua [video courtesy of Dev Sahni]

Joshua and Fury were unable to agree terms in 2021 and fight plans fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown has told Sky Sports he was uneasy about the delay in announcing the Joshua fight.

"Everybody's got a bit of doubt in their mind," he said. "There's reasons you could think that.

"If you'd asked me a week ago, I'd have said no, but now it's a little bit concerning that things haven't progressed down the line. We need to get this fight on."

Sports.title: 'Typical of Rory!' - Westwood hits back at McIlroy's LIV Golf comments
Sports.content:
Lee Westwood hit back at Rory McIlroy questioning the value of LIV golfers and claimed the comments were "typical" of the reigning Masters champion.

McIlroy warned ahead of the BMW Championship that it could be a "tough road back" for players wanting to return to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, with speculation ongoing around LIV Golf's long-term future.

Scottie Scheffler said some LIV Golf players could bring value to the PGA Tour if they return, although warned there should be penalties for any who come back, a notion McIlroy appeared to disagree with.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scottie Scheffler believes that a few LIV players would add value to the PGA Tour, but says they should still receive penalties before being integrated back in

"I would argue, have they brought value to LIV?" McIlroy told reporters earlier this week. He later added: "I feel like I've kept my position consistent that LIV has never been a good thing for the game."

Westwood will make his Legends Tour debut next week ahead of returning to the DP World Tour in October at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, with the Englishman one of multiple LIV Golf players to have accepted a sponsor's invitation.

"I really don't care what people think, to be perfectly honest," Westwood told TNT Sports at LIV Golf Indianapolis.

Image: Lee Westwood last featured at a DP World Tour event in 2023

"It [Alfred Dunhill Links Championship invite] illustrates the fact that people like LIV players in their events. Promoters and sponsors, no matter which tour they're on, they [LIV golfers] bring quality to tournaments.

"I heard Rory's comments. I thought Scottie [Scheffler] answered the question well and Rory's answer was just typical of Rory, really - it wasn't well thought out.

"There's a lot of players on this tour [LIV Golf] bring value to tournaments."

LIV Golf announced they have found an unnamed investor to help move into 'the next chapter', with chief executive Scott O'Neil warning they have a "very compressed timeline" to finalise funding to continue beyond the end of the 2026 season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau said in May that LIV Golf players were left 'surprised' by the Saudi Public Investment Fund's decision to withdraw funding

"Look, it's tough - it's not easy," said Bryson DeChambeau, who has yet to confirm whether he will extend his own LIV Golf contract. "We [LIV Golf] definitely have a lot against us.

"Behind the scenes, we've got a lot of people that are working hard to make this possible for not only all the players that are out here, but all the fans that have come out to these events.

"If it works, it works and that's awesome. If it doesn't, we'll figure things out and time will move on. I would say that time heals things. I hope people can see that we actually bring value to the game of golf. My wish is that people give us one more shot and be open-minded."

Sports.title: Antonelli fastest from Norris ahead of Sprint Qualifying as F1 returns
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Lando Norris in the only practice session at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.

Antonelli, who is 50 points ahead of Lewis Hamilton in the Drivers' Championship, continued where he left off by showing great pace throughout practice to better Norris by 0.121s and asserted himself as favourite for Sprint Qualifying later on Friday at 3.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1.

McLaren have brought upgrades to the rear of the car to complete the package that helped Norris to victory last time out in Hungary and are set to contend at the front again with Mercedes and Ferrari.

Although Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were fourth and fifth, Ferrari's new floor at Zandvoort appeared to be working well with both drivers within three tenths of Antonelli. The pair set their best lap times earlier than the Mercedes and McLarens, so, in theory, had a slower track.

George Russell was third and only 0.125s adrift of Antonelli as he looks to get his championship challenge back on track after a disappointing run of form before the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On The F1 Show podcast, David Croft questions whether Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can challenge Kimi Antonelli for this season's world championship

"It's tricky conditions. The wind is playing a factor and will continue to play a factor here," said Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok.

"But what was really interesting was that they were all within less than three tenths of a second at the top. That's really exciting for us as it shows that whatever work has gone on through the summer break, we've kind of carried on where we left off in Budapest.

"And I don't think we've seen the best of the Red Bulls in that session either yet."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract extension, George Russell and Lando Norris respond to questions about whether he ever posed a threat or caused concern

Oscar Piastri was unable to match Norris and finished six tenths back while the newly re-signed Max Verstappen at Red Bull was only 11th.

Verstappen was visibly struggling with the balance of his car and faces the prospect of a challenging final home event as the Dutch Grand Prix does not have a contract beyond this year.

Liam Lawson has replaced Isack Hadjar this weekend at Red Bull after the Frenchman suffered a wrist injury last week and was 14th, while Yuki Tsunoda, who has replaced Lawson at Racing Bulls, was 17th.

Pierre Gasly is running a big upgrade package on his car and was eighth for Alpine, splitting Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in seventh and Gabriel Bortoleto in ninth.

Aston Martin have engine and aerodynamic upgrades in Zandvoort, so Fernando Alonso finished 12th and 1.5 seconds off the pace - the closest they have been this season - and will hope to translate that pace into Sprint Qualifying later on.

Sports.title: Arsenal complete £51m Konsa deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £51m deal to sign defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

The England international has signed a four-year contract with the option of an additional 12 months after passing his medical, with only official confirmation of the deal remaining.

The 28-year-old could now make his Arsenal debut against his old club at Villa Park in the Monday Night Football on August 31, live on Sky Sports.

Aston Villa

Arsenal Monday 31st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Konsa has become Arsenal's fifth major summer signing after Piero Hincapie joined permanently from Bayer Leverkusen and the arrivals of Illan Meslier, Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes.

Konsa's arrival comes after the Premier League champions were looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for an extended period of time, while Jurrien Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

Villa had initially held out for £60m, with Arsenal hoping to pay much less, but the two clubs found a compromise on Thursday to strike a deal for the former Brentford defender.

Arsenal also looked into a potential move for Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah but have chosen to sign his England team-mate Konsa. Both players have a similar profile and can play at right-back and centre-back.

Image: Arsenal have completed a deal for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa

Analysis: Konsa is a perfect Arteta player - here's why

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

If there's one thing you need to know about Mikel Arteta, it's that he loves players that win duels. Nobody was better at it than Ezri Konsa last season.

He won more duels on the ground than any other Premier League player last season - finishing quite some distance ahead of his nearest challengers Virgil van Dijk and Gabriel - his new team-mate.

With both Saliba and Timber out injured, Arsenal were in need of a player who can cover both right-back and centre-back roles.

The Gunners do have Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White as cover in those roles - and both performed well in the Community Shield win over Manchester City - but the latter has a lengthy injury record over the last two seasons.

Arsenal also saw the importance of having good depth at right-back when Mosquera was forced to start the Champions League final with PSG out of position - with the young Spaniard conceding a penalty.

Now a move for Konsa has been completed, Arsenal have filled an important part of their team - and would be very close to completing their transfer window from an incomings point of view.

Can they find the forward player they have been looking for?

Sports.title: Billam-Smith expects Opetaia showdown in 2027
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith expects to fight Jai Opetaia next year, if they are both victorious in their upcoming bouts.

Former world champion Billam-Smith has long targeted Australia's Opetaia, widely regarded as the best cruiserweight in the sport.

Opetaia will box Noel Mikaelian on the undercard of Conor Benn's fight with Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas on September 12.

Billam-Smith should fight again before the end of the year and then intends to resume his pursuit of Opetaia.

It's a showdown he believes will happen in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Rozicki was pulled out of the fight after the seventh round following an instant classic with Chris Billam-Smith.

"I think so. I think I need to get through my next fight and then I'll fight the winner of that, whoever that might be," Billam-Smith told Sky Sports.

"Mikaelian on his day is a good fighter but I pick Jai to beat him.

"But it might take him a few rounds to set the pace and obviously Mikaelian's got some good names on his record, has some good performances but I feel like he's slowed down a little bit and gone a little bit past it now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Boxing commentary team watches on in disbelief as Ryan Rozicki takes some huge shots from opponent Chris Billam-Smith in their Zuffa Boxing 07 main event.

For his return to action Billam-Smith said: "Looking most probably around November time.

"I think it will be London or Bournemouth. Don't know who yet.

"The champions seem a bit tied up, I think [David] Benavidez is lining up a fight for December as well in Vegas, I believe."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke bounced back from being put down twice in the fourth round as he went on to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their cruiserweight classic.

Cheavon Clarke caught the eye with a knockout, comeback victory over Jack Massey on the undercard of Billam-Smith's barnstorming battle with Ryan Rozicki.

"Obviously Chev won on my undercard. He's got two [amateur] wins over me so from a competitor's point of view I'd very much like to get one back," Billam-Smith noted, speaking to Sky Sports at a screening of new boxing drama Fightland.

"[Clarke-Massey was] a superb fight which I think was definitely going to win fight of the night - until our fight."

Both Clarke and Massey were amateur foes of Billam-Smith's, and both of them beat the Bournemouth man in elite championship finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke recovered from being knocked down twice to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their enthralling clash.

He wants revenge. "I owe him one and I feel like that does the Jack Massey one in the ABA final as well. Both of those have beaten me in an ABA final. That would put that to bed so that would be nice," Billam-Smith said.

"I'm up for whoever," he added. "Zuffa are signing people all the time so you just don't know who's going to pop up out the woodwork and get offered. So we will see on that front."

Billam-Smith lost his WBO championship to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and beat Brandon Glanton in his only bout of last year. But June's thunderous collision with Rozicki showed that the 36-year-old can still perform in top-level contests.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Billam-Smith found out just how tough Ryan Rozicki was after the Canadian took nine clean shots from The Gentleman.

"I think if I'd taken my foot off the gas and was just sort of coasting I would definitely have been beat that night. I think that's the important thing to take away from my point of view," Billam-Smith said.

"I had to be switched on and pushing the training as I do and looking for different ways to improve.

"I'm on it. And I'm still getting better."

Fightland is coming to Sky and NOW on August 27.

Sports.title: Rise of Espanyol's English winger Dolan: 'I am not the player I was a year ago'
Sports.content:
Tyrhys Dolan made an explosive start to the season in LaLiga with a goal in Espanyol’s 3-0 win over Levante. The English forward looked particularly sharp. Something has changed. “I am not the person or player I was a year ago,” Dolan tells Sky Sports.

His first year in Spanish football after leaving Championship club Blackburn Rovers had its moments. He played against Real Madrid and Barcelona. But there is more to come, he insists. "I know the league now. I know myself a lot more. I know what I can do."

There is a reason for his optimism. Dolan spent much of last season operating on the right wing. "Pretty much on the touchline. Hanging wide." His job was to cross the ball and his numbers reflected that. "My assist output was much better than my goal output."

It was a learning experience that added to his repertoire. But now Dolan is back on the left. That role change brings new opportunities. "For me, it is better because I can cut in and get more shots off. I can be more dangerous as a left winger," he explains.

"Which way is he going to go?" he asks, imagining the dilemma facing the defender. "Is he going to take it and put across? Is he going to have a shot?" The change has already brought a goal. And it can bring more. "There are more avenues to my game."

Speaking to Dolan, 24, his enthusiasm for the challenge ahead is infectious. Last season turned into a slog for Espanyol after a strong start. They went from chasing Europe in the winter to the very real prospect of relegation in the spring. The slide was alarming.

"You'd be lying if you sit there and say you don't feel the energy around the stadium. We just don't want to have a repeat of that." That big win over Levante suggests something has changed. The buzz is back. "It was just like, yeah, now we're off and running again."

Image: Dolan celebrates his goals with a somersault

The summer has refreshed him. It was a chance to spend time with family and friends, important for a young man living alone in Barcelona. "Mentally, you need that switch off. Within the season, you are constantly preparing, dealing with emotions, good or bad."

He adds, poetically: "Absence, like they say, does make the heart grow fonder." It is why Espanyol spending much of pre-season in England was a boost. "My mum and dad were at every single game." But, encouragingly, part of him also missed his life in Barcelona.

"It was nice, that feeling, knowing that they were only an hour or so up the road," he says. "But for me, being in Barcelona means being in work mode and as an athlete you love it in that environment. You start missing it when you are away from it for too long."

Image: Dolan believes he is a different player to a year ago

Dolan has already shown in that game against Levante that he is ready to go again. "It was the perfect way to start. It is that reward for the hard work put in, a confidence boost for the team and obviously for myself too." But there are bigger tests ahead.

Espanyol host Real Madrid on Saturday evening in what will be the first game of the season in LaLiga for the 36-time champions of Spain. Jose Mourinho is back in charge. Kylian Mbappe, in Dolan's view, the best player he faced last season, will be there too.

He called that first meeting with Madrid a pinch-me moment. Now, it feels a little different. Still exciting, but he is approaching it with "a cooler head" and is unconcerned whether his opponent at right-back will be Trent Alexander-Arnold or Denzil Dumfries.

"Anybody. These are the games that you want to compete against the best so that you can bring your best and see where you are at." And his best is changing. "I was happy with what I did in my first season. But I know it is nowhere near what I know that I can do."

The challenge now is to show what he can do on the biggest stages and perhaps bring out that trademark somersault celebration against the world's most famous football club on Saturday. "I felt like I could give more for this team, for the club, for the supporters."

A chance to show that Tyrhys Dolan is a different player now.

The DBU said Infantino’s aborted proposal to sell commercial stakes in ⁠Fifa tournaments, including the ⁠World Cup, ​had created “a fundamental crisis of confidence in Fifa’s leadership” that could not be repaired by withdrawals or apologies. The DBU said it did not support ⁠Infantino in the 2023 presidential election and would not do so at the next election, which will take place at the 77th Fifa Congress in Rabat, Morocco, ⁠on March 18. “We are pleased that several federations are now withdrawing their support,” the DBU said in ​a statement after a board meeting. “DBU, together with ‌Uefa and our international colleagues, ‌will work to ensure that the member associations in the presidential election in 2027 have a ‌real choice and a credible alternative that can unite Fifa across confederations and rebuild the trust that has been broken.” Reuters Share

2h ago 06.15 EDT Iraola wants to add to 'quite thin' Liverpool squad Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola insists they will “definitely sign some players” after admitting his squad is still “quite thin”. The departures of Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate – plus the pending sale of Curtis Jones – have in no way been offset by the recruitment of Spain winger Victor Munoz and Rennes defender Jeremy Jacquet and a loan deal for fellow centre-back Ronald Araujo from Barcelona. They are light up front as, in addition to losing Salah’s significant contribution, striker Hugo Ekitike is sidelined for several months after surgery on an Achilles tendon injury. Liverpool had a £50million bid turned down for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh, who himself is likely to be sidelined for potentially three months after an operation on a leg injury sustained in pre-season, and reinforcing wide attacking areas remains their priority. Paris St Germain’s Bradley Barcola is their preferred option, although they disagree significantly on his valuation, but it is understood the club are looking at a number of possibilities to establish availability and test the market. “We will definitely sign some players. Some deals you have to wait until the end,” Iraola told Sky Sports. “But the end is the important picture, the one we will have on September 1, because it is true that we are still quite thin.” Liverpool look set to start Sunday’s match at Newcastle with Jacquet, whose pre-season amounted to only 45 minutes of last weekend’s friendly against Como, in central defence and the primarily left-sided 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha on the right. Housewives’ favourite Luke Entwistle has the answer. double quotation mark On the eve of a new Ligue 1 season, many clubs seem a little distracted. Even those accustomed to competing at the top have concerns that transcend the pitch. In a league that contains the greatest team on the continent, the focus of the majority of clubs has shifted to surviving and providing, rather than competing. Any fighting spirit has long since been kicked out of Paris Saint-Germain’s competitors; back-to-back Champions League titles will do that. It feels like a long time ago since Kylian Mbappé moved to Real Madrid on a free transfer, leaving behind a scent of opportunity that filled the nostrils of Marseille, Monaco and Lille. Roberto De Zerbi was bullish when he joined Marseille. “I’m not here to finish second,” said the manager, who has since moved to Tottenham. Finishing second has now become an aspiration, especially for a club such as Marseille, given their predicament. PSG are the best team in Europe. Rose told a press conference: “The things I saw so far with Chelsea and now Manchester City, it’s a clear idea, a clear philosophy. You know what you get, you know what they want to play, you see the processes and the approach they have. It’s quite intense against the ball, high pressing and, with the ball, you know what quality you face and you see a clear idea in established play. “It’s a tough challenge but we are quite positive. We had a really good pre-season. I settled in very well and everyone supported me and the new coaching staff.” The Cherries lost forward Junior Kroupi to a foot injury during pre-season, but scored 22 goals across five friendly fixtures this summer. “Everyone put a lot of effort into the preparation and all the things around so we feel well prepared for the upcoming season and for the game against Manchester City,” Rose added ahead of his Premier League bow.
