World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. That included 506,000 from abroad, which was also the highest ever figure, with Brits, Israelis and Americans the most common foreign visitors https://t.co/6yMrRcf6ml — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 28, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.title: FedEx-led €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost wins EU approval
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Tesco Teams Up With Wolt. Can Express Delivery Save Its Czech Business?
World.content:
Tesco will launch a new express delivery service in Prague in September, working with Wolt to deliver orders within 40 minutes.

The service, called Tesco Hned, will initially be available from selected Tesco stores in the Czech capital.

The launch comes as speculation continues over a possible sale of Tesco’s Central European operations and the British retailer’s future in the Czech Republic.



Tesco Hned is designed for customers who need groceries and other everyday products quickly rather than as part of a larger planned shop. Orders will include food, drinks, cosmetics, household products, pet supplies and other goods.

The company says its standard online shopping service will continue to focus on larger orders, while the new option is aimed at customers who need a few items immediately.

Tesco has already tested the service at six Prague stores. It plans to extend Tesco Hned to another 22 locations in the coming weeks.

Delivery will be provided through Wolt, giving customers access to Tesco products through the courier company’s platform.

Tesco faces questions over its future

The new service comes at a difficult time for Tesco in Central Europe.

According to the Financial Times, Tesco’s British owners are considering selling their operations in the region, including the Czech Republic. The Schwarz Group, which owns Lidl and Kaufland, and Polish retailer Biedronka have reportedly been mentioned among potential buyers.

Tesco has not announced plans to leave the Czech market, and the launch of Tesco Hned suggests the company continues to invest in its services.

World.title: New Budget Airline to Launch Direct Flights from Prague to Santiago de Compostela
World.content:
A new budget airline is set to launch direct flights between Prague and Santiago de Compostela in Spain, giving travellers from the Czech capital a new low-cost option for visiting Galicia and the famous Camino de Santiago.

Fly2Galicia plans to begin operating flights from Santiago–Rosalía de Castro Airport to eight European destinations from December 1, 2026.



Prague is among the international destinations, alongside Brussels, Munich, Venice and Milan.

Tickets are already on sale, with fares from Prague to Santiago de Compostela starting at €51.

The new route could be particularly attractive in 2027, when Santiago de Compostela will celebrate a Holy Year. The occasion is expected to bring increased numbers of pilgrims completing the Camino de Santiago, one of Europe’s best-known pilgrimage routes.

There is, however, one detail to note: Fly2Galicia will not operate the initial flights itself. The airline says the routes will be operated by another European carrier, which has not yet been named.

The new service comes as airlines continue to expand connections between Central Europe and Spain. Wizz Air has also announced new flights to Santiago from Rome and Warsaw starting this December.

What to see in Santiago de Compostela

For travellers arriving from Prague, Santiago’s historic centre is the main attraction. Its UNESCO-listed Old Town combines Romanesque, Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical architecture, with the Cathedral of Santiago at the heart of the city.

The Mercado de Abastos is another popular stop, offering fresh seafood and local produce. Galicia is also known for Albariño, a white wine that pairs particularly well with the region’s seafood.

Santiago can also serve as a base for exploring Galicia, with trips to A Coruña, Vigo and the Rías Baixas wine region, as well as the area’s beaches and islands.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: Students in Czech Republic Face Higher Rents as Housing Costs Rise
World.content:
Students looking for private accommodation in Czech university cities this year are facing higher rents, with prices for some types of housing up by as much as 14 percent compared with 2025.

The increase comes as demand for student accommodation reaches its annual peak ahead of the winter semester.

Data from several Czech property platforms show that the busiest period started earlier this year, meaning students who have not yet found accommodation may face a more limited and expensive selection in September.

Those unable to secure a place in a student dormitory generally have three alternatives: renting a small apartment alone, taking a private room in a shared apartment, or renting a bed in shared accommodation.



The most expensive option is usually a small one-bedroom apartment with a kitchenette, typically around 30 square meters. According to the REMAX network, monthly rents for these apartments range from more than CZK 7,000 in Ústí nad Labem to around CZK 14,000 in Prague.

Prices have not increased evenly across the country. Brno recorded the sharpest rise, with rents for small apartments increasing by 12 percent year on year.

Prague saw a 4 percent increase, while rents in Hradec Králové and Pardubice rose by almost 9 percent. Olomouc was one of the few exceptions, with prices falling by slightly more than 2 percent.

Rent is not the only expense students need to consider. Utilities, water and maintenance charges can add another CZK 1,000 to CZK 2,000 a month, according to property platforms.

Private rooms offer a cheaper alternative

Many students instead rent individual rooms in shared apartments, with properties ranging from smaller 2+kk and 2+1 layouts to larger 4+kk and 4+1 apartments. Czech property portal Sreality.cz puts the average cost of a private room in university cities at between approximately CZK 5,700 in Opava and CZK 11,500 in Prague.

In Prague, private rooms listed on Sreality.cz were around 10 percent more expensive than during the same period last year. Prices in Brno, meanwhile, remained roughly unchanged.

Shared housing remains the cheapest option

For students on a tighter budget, sharing an apartment and renting a bed rather than an entire room remains the least expensive choice. The more people share a property, the lower the individual housing costs tend to be.

Even this option, however, has become more expensive. According to UlovDomov.cz, the cost of renting a bed has increased by several hundred Czech crowns compared with last year.

Prague remains considerably more expensive. A bed in a two-bedroom apartment costs almost CZK 5,500, about CZK 1,200 more than a bed in a three-bedroom apartment.

World.title: 58 Years Since Warsaw Pact Troops Invaded Czechoslovakia
World.content:
On August 21, 1968, Soviet troops and their Warsaw Pact allies invaded Czechoslovakia to bring an end to that country’s brief period of political liberalization, called the Prague Spring.

People still recall waking up on that fateful morning to find that Soviet-led Warsaw Pact tanks had rolled into the country, crushing all hope of implementing the democratic reforms of the Prague Spring. Shocked citizens took to the streets in protest of the invasion.

About 500,000 troops were involved in the invasion and occupation, during which 137 Czechoslovaks died and some 500 were wounded.

One of the key battles was for the control of Czech Radio, similar to the one that took place at the end of the Second World War.

The invasion ended the political and economic reforms led by Alexander Dubcek and reasserted dominant Soviet and Communist authority in Czechoslovakia.

It also helped establish the Brezhnev Doctrine, which Moscow said allowed the U.S.S.R. to intervene in any country where a communist government was under threat.

Within the following year, resistance faded, Dubček was removed from office, his reforms were undone, and a more Soviet-controlled government was installed.

World.title: Prague’s Groovy Market Fest Returns After a Successful Debut
World.content:
A new urban festival is aiming to become a regular fixture on Prague’s cultural calendar after attracting 1,200 visitors to its first edition in Riegrovy sady.

Groovy Market Fest, held on August 1, brought together food, design, music and local brands in a format inspired by European city markets.

According to the organizers, around 85% of visitors were tourists or foreign residents of Prague, highlighting the event’s appeal beyond the Czech-speaking audience.



The festival will return to Riegrovy sady on September 5, with further editions planned for October, November and December.

From Barcelona to Prague

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food culture.

Their interest in international gastronomy also led them to compete in Spain. In 2025, they won first place in the Cooking The Street competition, where their dish was judged by a professional panel that included chefs Beñat Ormaetxea and Jon Kepa Aurrecoetxea.

After returning to Prague, they decided to develop their own event, drawing inspiration from markets such as Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market.

The First Edition

Food Garden focused on gastronomy, while Palm Street featured local products and handmade goods. The Design Zone presented Czech brands working in fashion, design and art.

Rather than filling the site with as many vendors as possible, the organizers selected a smaller number of participants. They say the approach was intended to create a more coherent experience for visitors.

Music was another part of the programme, with live performances and DJ sets throughout the event. Visitors could also attend a masterclass focused on preparing the festival’s signature Groovy cocktail.

Additional editions are scheduled for October 3, November 7 and December 5, all at the same location.

Tickets for upcoming editions are available through GoOut.

World.title: Faster Than the Metro. New Bus is Now Linking Prague 8 and Prague 6
World.content:
A new bus service running through Prague’s Blanka tunnel has begun operating, offering a direct connection between the northern part of the city and Dejvice.

Bus line 145 connects Čimice and Kobylisy in Prague 8 with Hradčanská and Dejvická in Prague 6. The journey takes around 15 minutes, according to Prague’s public transport authority ROPID.



The same trip by metro requires a change between lines C and A in the city centre and takes around 22 minutes.

Including the time spent walking through stations and using escalators, the journey can take about half an hour.

The first day of operation brought mostly positive results, with many buses arriving on time or even ahead of schedule. The real test will come during regular weekday traffic, when congestion around Prague is heavier.

Where the new bus runs

In the direction from Čimice to Dejvice, line 145 serves:

Sídliště Čimice – Čimice – Libeňská – Řepínská – Podhajská pole – Čimický háj – Písečná – Služská – Kobylisy – Okrouhlická – Vychovatelna – Hradčanská – Vítězné náměstí – Dejvická

The return route follows the same corridor in the opposite direction.

The key feature of line 145 is its use of the Blanka tunnel, allowing buses to avoid the city centre and provide a direct connection between Prague 8 and Prague 6.

The new route is expected to make commuting easier for residents of Čimice, Kobylisy and surrounding neighbourhoods, while providing an alternative to the metro for journeys towards Dejvice and Hradčanská.

World.title: Leo Express to Launch Direct Prague–Brno Trains in December
World.content:
Leo Express is set to begin operating direct trains between Prague and Brno in December, marking the private carrier’s first direct connection between the two cities.

The company has already been serving passengers in the South Moravian Region, but its trains have so far bypassed Brno.

Over the past year, travellers from towns such as Hodonín and Břeclav have been able to use Leo Express services to reach Prague, travelling via Přerov and Olomouc.



The new Prague–Brno service will change that, putting the carrier directly on one of the Czech Republic’s busiest rail routes.

There is, however, one limitation for passengers travelling to Prague.

Leo Express trains do not serve Prague Main Station. In Prague, passengers must use Praha-Libeň station, which may be less convenient for those travelling to the city centre.

Leo Express was founded by businessman Leoš Novotný and has operated passenger trains in the Czech Republic since 2012.

The company has gradually expanded its network in the Czech Republic and abroad, competing with established operators such as České dráhy and RegioJet.

The Prague–Brno connection is expected to become another important part of the company’s Czech network from December.

World.title: Hungarian man causes hundreds of thousands of euros in damage in Austria in car theft spree
World.content:
A 49-year-old Hungarian man has been arrested in Austria on suspicion of breaking into cars and stealing valuable vehicle parts in at least 60 cases across five provinces, according to Austrian police. The total damage caused by the alleged offences could amount to several hundred thousand euros.

Suspect caught red-handed near Vienna

The man was arrested in Brunn am Gebirge, after police caught him carrying previously removed light modules and bonnets from a car dealership to his vehicle parked nearby.

This incident alone is estimated to have caused around EUR 15,000 in damage.

The investigation began on 8 July after several vehicles were broken into at a car rental company’s premises in Graz. Criminal investigators subsequently identified around 60 similar cases across Styria, Burgenland, Vienna, Lower Austria and Upper Austria.

Police tracked suspect across Austria

According to the Hungarian News Agency (MTI), investigators eventually identified a vehicle they believed may have been connected to several of the offences. This lead helped them identify the Hungarian suspect. Police also discovered that the man had previously been convicted in Hungary for property-related offences.

At the beginning of August, investigators established that the suspect had returned to Austria. He was subsequently observed near car dealerships and company car parks, among other locations.

On the evening of 18 August, the 49-year-old crossed into Austria again at Klingenbach in Burgenland. Police followed him to an industrial area in Brunn am Gebirge, where he reportedly used an electric scooter to scout the area. The following night, Austrian officers moved in as he was carrying the previously removed vehicle parts towards his car.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Man admits only latest alleged offence

During questioning, the Hungarian suspect admitted to the offence in Brunn am Gebirge but denied the other allegations. Police said the investigation into the remaining cases and any possible connections between them is still ongoing.

The Styrian State Police Directorate said the suspected offences caused damage amounting to several hundred thousand euros in total.

World.title: Adelaide Bridge shines in Hungarian colours for 20 August – photos, video
World.content:
The Riverbank Precinct Pedestrian Bridge over the River Torrens in Adelaide was illuminated in red, white and green on 20 August to celebrate Hungary’s National Day.

The special illumination brought together a large number of members of South Australia’s Hungarian community, along with families and friends, for an evening of celebration and togetherness.

The event was honoured by the presence of The Hon Joe Szakacs MP, South Australia’s Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, who joined the community and addressed the gathering. Minister Szakacs, who has Hungarian heritage, was warmly welcomed by those attending.

Mr Attila Szabó, Honorary Consul of Hungary in South Australia, also attended and addressed the community.

Hungary’s 20 August national day celebrated in Adelaide, Australia. Photo: László Czár

As darkness fell, the Hungarian colours lit up the bridge and were reflected beautifully across the River Torrens, creating a spectacular sight for those gathered along the riverbank.

The evening included Hungarian food, community fellowship and an opportunity for Hungarian families and friends to celebrate their heritage together in the heart of Adelaide.

Hungary’s 20 August national day celebrated in Adelaide, Australia. Photo: László Czár Hungary’s 20 August national day celebrated in Adelaide, Australia. Photo: László Czár

The successful celebration was made possible through the support and cooperation of the South Australian Department for Infrastructure and Transport, the Minister’s office, the Hungarian Consulate and the local Hungarian community.

For one special evening, the colours of Hungary proudly shone over the River Torrens. Éljen Magyarország!

World.title: Dramatic car chase at Lake Balaton: Police shoot at driver after he tries to run them down
World.content:
A dramatic police chase unfolded at Lake Balaton on 20 August after a driver who was initially stopped near Aszófő allegedly sped away, crashed into several police vehicles and tried to hit officers on a cycle path. Four police officers suffered minor injuries, while the driver was taken to hospital.

Lake Balaton car chase: Driver fled after police tried to stop him

Police received a report late on Thursday afternoon that a car was travelling erratically on main road 71, near kilometre 58. Officers stopped the vehicle at the Aszófő rest area, but the driver suddenly accelerated away towards the centre of Tihany. He subsequently collided with a police vehicle.

Officers attempted to stop him again in Tihany, but the man drove onto a cycle path, where he allegedly tried to run over police officers who were there. Police then fired targeted shots at the vehicle’s tyres in an attempt to bring it to a halt.

Car continued despite damaged tyres

The shooting did not immediately end the chase. Despite its damaged tyres, the vehicle continued at high speed. The driver was again confronted by police in Balatonfüred, where the car collided with a police vehicle before speeding away. Shortly afterwards, it struck another police vehicle.

The pursuit finally came to an end when the car crashed into an electricity pole. According to police, the driver had continuously endangered other road users as well as the lives and physical safety of pedestrians and cyclists during the escape.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Four officers suffered minor injuries

Four police officers sustained minor injuries during the operation, while the driver was also taken to hospital. Police said an investigation into all the circumstances of the incident is ongoing.

The dramatic chase took place on Hungary’s national holiday, when the Lake Balaton region was particularly busy with visitors and holidaymakers.

World.title: PHOTOS, VIDEOS: Budapest lights up as Hungary celebrates 20 August with spectacular fireworks and drone show
World.content:
Budapest was transformed into a spectacular open-air show on Thursday evening as thousands gathered along the Danube to celebrate Hungary’s national holiday. This year’s 20 August celebrations combined fireworks with a large-scale drone display, laser effects and illuminated projections bringing Hungarian history to life across some of the capital’s most iconic landmarks.

Budapest’s skyline becomes a giant history book

The evening’s main spectacle began shortly after 9 PM, with a spectacular light show projected onto the Hungarian Parliament and surrounding buildings. Images and scenes inspired by Hungary’s history appeared on the façades of buildings, the Chain Bridge and other landmarks, accompanied by music and laser effects.

The production, titled Chapters from the 1,000-Year History of the Hungarian Nation, took audiences on a journey from the natural landscapes of the Carpathian Basin through the arrival of the Hungarians and the foundation of the Hungarian state to themes of freedom and light.

The show drew inspiration from Hungarian art, architecture and historical motifs. Among the images featured were elements inspired by the Feszty Panorama, the Coronation Mantle, medieval seals and medallions, as well as works by celebrated Hungarian painters Gyula Benczúr and Bertalan Székely.

Around 2,000 drones filled the sky

One of the most striking additions to this year’s celebrations was the huge drone display above the Danube. Around 2,000 drones formed different shapes and images in the night sky, complementing the projections and lasers and giving the traditional 20 August spectacle a distinctly modern touch.

The show was also considerably shorter than in previous years, with the fireworks themselves lasting around ten minutes. Instead, organisers placed greater emphasis on the drone and light elements. The result was a more varied spectacle, combining technology with imagery drawn from Hungary’s cultural and historical heritage.

Photo: Anadolu Agency Photo: Anadolu Agency Photo: Anadolu Agency

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Crowds packed the Danube waterfront

Large crowds gathered along both sides of the Danube to watch the celebrations, with particularly large numbers of spectators around the Parliament and the city centre. The sheer number of people heading home after the event even caused temporary disruption to public transport, with the M2 metro line temporarily closed amid the crowds.

Despite strong winds and lightning visible on the horizon, the storm fortunately did not disrupt the main evening programme.

The celebrations were also notable for marking the first 20 August national holiday under Hungary’s new political era following the end of the previous government’s 16-year rule.

President András Baka delivered his national holiday address before the fireworks began.

A smaller celebration with a new look

The government had promised a more modest 20 August programme this year. According to figures cited by Hungarian media, the celebrations were organised with a budget of around HUF 4 billion (EUR 11 million), compared with approximately HUF 17.5 billion (EUR 48 million) last year.

Organisers nevertheless sought to retain the best-known elements of the traditional celebrations while adding contemporary features. For those who wanted to avoid the crowds, parts of the light show were repeated later in the evening, although the fireworks and drone display were not repeated.

Take a look through our photo gallery below for some of the most spectacular moments from Budapest’s 20 August celebrations.

World.title: President Zelensky invites PM Magyar to Kyiv for a long-awaited meeting
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has invited Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar to Kyiv, which signals a possible new chapter in relations between the two neighbouring countries. The invitation came in a letter marking Hungary’s national holiday on 20 August.

The Ukrainian president sent a letter to Hungary

Volodymyr Zelensky congratulated Magyar and the Hungarian people on St Stephen’s Day, saying Ukraine and Hungary are connected by centuries of good-neighbourly relations, mutual respect and shared struggles for freedom and statehood.

In the letter, published by the Ukrainian Embassy in Budapest, Zelensky thanked Hungary for what he described as consistent support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as solidarity during Russia’s invasion. He specifically highlighted humanitarian assistance, support for the rehabilitation of Ukrainian children and soldiers, and help provided to Ukrainian citizens.

Zelensky: a new chapter could begin

Zelensky described Hungary as a “good neighbour and reliable partner”, saying the outcome of Hungary’s recent election could open a new chapter in bilateral relations. According to the Ukrainian president, the new phase should be based on mutually beneficial cooperation, mutual respect, peace and understanding.

The timing is also significant, as Ukraine and Hungary are marking the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year. Zelensky said he was ready to strengthen open and constructive cooperation between the two countries and develop closer ties towards their “common European future”.

He then extended a direct invitation to Magyar. “I would welcome you in Kyiv at the nearest suitable time for you,” Zelensky wrote. He also wished Magyar success in building a modern Hungarian state and wished the Hungarian people peace, unity and prosperity.

A meeting has already been discussed

A bilateral meeting between Magyar and Zelensky has been under discussion for months. In early July, on his way to the NATO summit in Ankara, Magyar said he had held a brief meeting with Zelensky the previous day. The two reportedly agreed to hold formal bilateral talks in the near future.

At the time, Budapest or Kyiv were discussed as possible venues, followed by a joint visit to Transcarpathia, including Berehove. Magyar had indicated that he wanted to visit Berehove on his first official trip to Ukraine. Zelensky’s latest letter therefore puts Kyiv firmly on the table as the venue for the next stage of talks.

Stay up-to-date: Rubio praises US-Hungary ties as Orbán, Karácsony deliver starkly different messages on 20 August holiday

Ukraine’s prime minister also invites Magyar

As 24.hu writes, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi also sent a St Stephen’s Day message to his Hungarian counterpart. According to the Ukrainian Embassy, Koretskyi congratulated Magyar, thanked Hungary for its support for Ukraine’s sovereignty, welcomed the resumption of dialogue and called for closer bilateral cooperation.

World.title: Severe storms threaten several regions in Hungary, heat to peak today
World.content:
Hungary is set to endure its hottest day of the week on Friday, with temperatures potentially reaching 38°C, while severe thunderstorms and torrential rain could hit several parts of the country.

According to HungaroMet, temperatures will climb to between 31°C and 38°C during the hottest hours of Friday. The north-western and northern parts of the country are expected to see showers and thunderstorms, despite generally sunny conditions with high and cumulus clouds.

The biggest risk of severe weather will be in Transdanubia, where thunderstorms could bring torrential downpours and powerful winds. Strong south-westerly and westerly winds are also expected west of the Tisza River. Around thunderstorms, gusts could become storm-force or even exceptionally strong.

Heat peaks on Friday

The hottest conditions are expected away from the north-western border, where temperatures may be a few degrees lower. Elsewhere, the mercury could rise as high as 38°C.

The heat has already prompted the national chief medical officer to issue a second-degree heat alert across the whole of Hungary. The warning came into force at midnight on Thursday and will remain in place until midnight on Sunday.

People spending time outdoors are advised to take precautions against the extreme heat, particularly during the hottest part of the afternoon.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Temperatures ease slightly over the weekend

The heat will begin to ease on Saturday, although temperatures will remain high. Western Hungary is expected to be cloudier, while sunnier conditions will prevail in the east. A few showers or thunderstorms could still develop in the north-east. The north-westerly wind will strengthen in several areas.

Temperatures will range from 16°C to 25°C in the early morning and 25°C to 37°C in the afternoon.

Sunday will bring a more settled picture, with sunshine accompanied by high and cumulus clouds and little chance of rain. Northerly winds may strengthen in some areas. Morning temperatures are expected to range from 15°C to 20°C, while afternoon highs will fall to 25°C–32°C nationwide.

From scorching heat to stormy weather

Friday is therefore likely to bring a sharp contrast across Hungary: near-40°C heat in some areas alongside potentially severe thunderstorms, torrential rain and powerful wind gusts. The weekend should gradually become cooler and drier, with the most significant relief arriving by Sunday.

World.title: Hungary’s famous Miskolctapolca Cave Bath finally reopens after almost two years
World.content:
The famous Miskolctapolca Barlangfürdő (or Miskolctapolca Cave Bath) has reopened after a two-year closure, following a major reconstruction costing around HUF 1.5 billion. The reopening is an important step in restoring tourism to one of Miskolc’s best-known attractions.

One of the most popular baths in the country finally reopened

The Miskolctapolca Cave Bath officially reopened on Thursday, 20 August, two years after an electrical fault caused a fire at the complex. The blaze started in the Aquatherapy section before spreading to the roof structure of the main building, destroying around 800 square metres. No one was injured. The subsequent investigation determined that an electrical malfunction had caused the fire.

The bath, which is housed partly in rare natural cave passages, is one of the region’s most distinctive tourist attractions. Around HUF 1.5 billion (approximately EUR 4,11 million) has been spent on its reconstruction and modernisation.

Visitors at Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of its grand reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János

“A safer and more sustainable Cave Bath”

At the reopening ceremony, Miskolc Mayor József Tóth-Szántai said the reopening would partly restore the normality disrupted by the fire two years ago. “With the opening of the facility, residents and visitors are getting back a safer, more modern and sustainable Miskolctapolca Cave Bath,” the mayor said.

He described the period since the fire as a long and difficult journey and thanked everyone involved in the reconstruction for their dedication. The reopening was also welcomed as an important moment for Miskolctapolca, whose tourism industry suffered significantly during the closure.

Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of its grand reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János Visitors at Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of its grand reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János

Tourism can finally return to Miskolctapolca

András Czipa, a Tisza Party MP, said that after the fire, Miskolctapolca had become noticeably quieter. The crowds of tourists and long queues that had once characterised the area were replaced by empty streets, affecting not only the bath itself but also accommodation providers, restaurants and other local businesses. He said the reopening means that “life is returning to Miskolctapolca”.

The restoration is not yet completely finished, however. The medical treatment section of the complex is currently not operating. In the meantime, arrangements have been made to ensure that therapeutic massage and physiotherapy remain available elsewhere in Miskolc.

Czipa said professional and political discussions were already under way about the future development strategy for the Cave Bath. He stressed that the issue should not be viewed through party politics, but rather in terms of what can help Miskolc move forward.

Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of its grand reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János Miskolctapolca Cave Bath on the day of its grand reopening. Photo: MTI/Vajda János

A new beginning for a famous attraction

Czipa described the reopening as a new beginning, with the aim of creating a bath that preserves the features that made it unique and internationally famous while also allowing it to develop and attract visitors once again. The return of tourists could provide an important boost to local businesses, creating jobs and generating new revenue for the area.

The scale of the disruption caused by the fire had raised concerns about the future of Miskolctapolca as a tourist destination. Following the disaster, the city opened a dedicated bank account to receive donations towards rebuilding the Cave Bath.

The reopening therefore represents not only the return of a major attraction but also a significant step towards restoring the wider tourism economy around it.

In case you missed it: Hungary overhauls tourism as Minister Kapitány announces three major appointments

A packed programme celebrates the reopening

The reopening coincides with a four-day programme titled “Pezsgés Miskolctapolcán” (“Buzz in Miskolctapolca”), featuring concerts, food and community events along Babits Promenade near the entrance to the bath.

At Miskolc Airport, the “Legends in the Air” event runs from Thursday to Saturday, offering air displays, unusual aircraft, family activities and a performance by Hungarian aerobatic pilot Péter Bessenyei.

The city centre is hosting the “Shining Light Festival” on Thursday and Friday, with light installations and projections displayed on public spaces and buildings. On Saturday evening, runners will take part in the Night Run Miskolc, starting from Szent István Square, with 5 km, 10 km and half-marathon distances available.

For Miskolctapolca, however, the most significant event of the weekend is undoubtedly the return of the attraction at the heart of its tourism industry: after two difficult years, the Cave Bath is open again.

World.title: Rubio praises US-Hungary ties as Orbán, Karácsony deliver starkly different messages on 20 August holiday
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised the strong partnership between the United States and Hungary in a message marking Hungary’s national holiday, published on the State Department’s website on Thursday.

Rubio noted that 20 August was a reminder “of the historic ties between our peoples”. “The friendship between the United States and Hungary rests on the foundation of a mutual respect for sovereignty, proud heritage, and the hard-won liberties that define our two republics,” he added.

“Today, the United States reaffirms its strong and forward-looking partnership with Hungary, one sustained by deep economic ties, shared security interests, and a commitment to the values that have long united the West,” Rubio wrote.

Karácsony wishes Hungary happy ‘rebirthday’ on national holiday

Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony marked the 20 August national holiday on Thursday by wishing Hungary a “happy rebirthday” and highlighted the need to strengthen the resilience of Hungary and Budapest.

“Happy birthday, Hungary! But perhaps, here and now, it would be more accurate to say: happy rebirthday, Hungary!’ Karácsony said in a video on his YouTube channel, noting that an overwhelming majority had voted for a “European Hungary” in the April election.

Speaking about the challenges facing the country, Karácsony noted that the water level of the Danube had never been so low, the summer had never been so hot or so dry, and the country’s water and electricity supplies had never been so close to collapse as during this summer.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

The heat, the drought and their serious consequences will not be exceptions, but the new norm in Hungary, and in Budapest in particular, he said. The number of hot days is steadily rising, and “we are having to contend with prolonged droughts or sudden floods”, which are affecting agriculture, housing, transport, health and the social situation, he said.

The sight of the Danube, Lake Velence, Lake Balaton, the rivers and streams, the arable fields and the parks had perhaps made it clear to everyone that this was not merely a scientific prediction, nor was it scaremongering, he said. Constant adaptation, as well as strengthening the resilience of the country and of Budapest – which is particularly vulnerable to climate change – is the responsibility of the government, the capital, all Hungarian local authorities and every Hungarian citizen, he added.

Orbán: ‘We were, we are, we will be’

“We were, we are, we will be. Happy birthday, Hungary!” opposition Fidesz leader Viktor Orbán said in a post on Facebook on Thursday to mark the 20 August national holiday. In his post, the former prime minister shared a music video for the song Megmaradni magyarnak (To Remain Hungarian) by the band Kiss Kata, commenting: “It’s a beautiful song, thank you!”

Meanwhile, János Bóka, Fidesz’s parliamentary group leader, pledged to uphold Hungary’s cross-border community, the family, sovereignty, and a self-sustaining economy, and to resist “autocracy” and the “selling out of the country”. “St Stephen’s work holds timeless lessons,” Bóka said in a video posted on Facebook, marking the national holiday. “I believe that our cross-border community is an asset which survived the 20th century and must be preserved in the 21st century as well.”

He called for resistance against “autocracy”, defence of Hungarian families and values, and solidarity with Hungarians beyond the borders. “We must distinguish truth from falsehood, appearance from reality… Hungary and its people can count on us,” he said. Bóka stressed that Hungary’s fate is tied to Christian Europe, where its peace and prosperity must be secured.

World.title: Less than half of Romanians manage to save regularly, survey finds
World.content:
Roughly 48% of Romanians are able to put away money every month or most months, while a quarter manage to put money aside only occasionally, when they have funds left, according to a survey conducted at the initiative of tbi bank on a sample of 1,223 employees nationwide.

The survey, published on Friday, August 21, shows that Romanians’ real savings capacity remains limited and vulnerable to increasing pressures on the monthly budget.

Roughly 22% of respondents currently do not save at all or are forced to draw on previously accumulated reserves. Moreover, about 46% manage to save no more than RON 500 in a typical month, and 16% are unable to set aside any money at all.

The ability to save remains moderate even among those who manage to put money aside: almost 22% save between 11% and 20% of income, and just over 22% manage to keep between 6% and 10%.

“For many Romanians, saving remains the result of a fragile balance at the end of the month rather than a consistent financial plan. The increase in essential costs limits the amounts available, and this makes financial discipline, access to simple and safe products and the formation of savings habits increasingly important,” said Gergana Staykova, Market Leader, tbi bank Romania.

The ability to save has deteriorated for an important part of Romanians in the last period. Almost 42% say they save less than last year, and over 9% managed to put money aside previously, but currently they can no longer do so. At the same time, more than 29% save primarily for unforeseen situations or emergencies, and about 20% aim to build more security and financial independence.

Over 36% say they save only what they have left after covering expenses, while only about 15% set aside a fixed percentage of their monthly income. At the same time, almost 23% could cover their expenses for less than a month if they lost their main source of income, and about 22% could cover their expenses for between one and three months.

Romanians keep their savings mainly in forms perceived as safe and easy to access. Over 23% keep most of their savings in their current account, and almost 22% choose bank deposits. At the same time, more than 26% point to the increase in the price of food and basic products as the main obstacle to saving, and almost 25% say that income is too low in relation to expenses.

Savings are used both for planned experiences and needs, and as a reserve for unforeseen expenses. Almost 19% of Romanians have used or would have liked to use their savings for vacations and personal experiences, and over 14% for home or car repairs. The financial targets for 2026 are mainly geared towards strengthening reserves and protecting personal stability, amid fears related in particular to health and income. Almost 20% of Romanians aim to save more than last year, and almost 15% want to protect their existing savings. At the same time, more than 30% point to health problems as their biggest financial fear, and 21% primarily fear losing their job.

The tbi bank survey on how Romanians manage their money in 2026 was conducted online in July this year, on a total sample of 1,223 internet users in Romania, of which over 53% are men, 68% work in the private sector, and over 31% have a net income of over RON 6,000.

World.title: Romania’s real estate investment volume falls to EUR 300 million in H1 2026 - report
World.content:
Romania’s real estate investment market recorded transactions worth approximately EUR 300 million in the first half of 2026, down from around EUR 400 million in the same period last year, according to a Colliers report. The consultancy estimates that the full-year volume could approach EUR 1 billion if several large transactions currently underway are completed.

Romania accounted for roughly 5% of the EUR 5.8 billion invested across the six largest Central and Eastern European economies: Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia.

Regional investment increased by 7% year-on-year and exceeded both the five-year average of EUR 4.6 billion and the ten-year average of EUR 5.1 billion. Colliers expects the regional total to reach EUR 12.5-13 billion in 2026, compared with EUR 11.6 billion last year.

“The decline in transaction volumes in Romania during the period under review should be seen in a broader context,” said Robert Miklo, partner and head of capital markets at Colliers.

He noted that several deals are in progress, while the sale of a MAS retail portfolio to AFI Europe was completed shortly after the end of the reporting period, shifting the transaction into the third quarter.

“If other large transactions currently in progress are also completed, 2026 has the potential to close with investment volumes of close to EUR 1 billion, which would make it only the second year since 2007 in which the market has reached this threshold,” Miklo said.

Office properties generated approximately 60% of Romania’s transaction volume during the first half, their highest share since 2022. Colliers expects that percentage to decline as major deals in other sectors are completed during the remainder of the year.

“Influenced by the limited supply of properties available for sale, investment volumes remain below the level suggested by both investor appetite and the size of the local economy. In the first half of the year, Romania attracted just 5.4% of the investment volume recorded across the six largest economies in the region, despite accounting for almost 18% of their combined GDP. This gap shows that the local market still has substantial room for growth,” added Robert Miklo.

In Bucharest, prime yields stood at approximately 7.5% for offices, 7.75% for industrial and logistics properties, and 7.25% for shopping centers. These levels remained above those recorded in Warsaw, Prague, and Bratislava.

Colliers said investors are increasingly prioritizing assets with stable income, good energy performance, and clear long-term value prospects. Properties with weaker energy performance face tighter lending standards and lower demand.

“Financing conditions are favorable, but the advantage lies with high-quality properties with stable income, credible sponsors, and clear sustainability strategies,” Miklo said.

Across Central and Eastern Europe, Poland led the market with more than EUR 3 billion in transactions, representing 52% of the regional total. The Czech Republic followed with more than EUR 1.4 billion, while Hungary recorded close to EUR 600 million.

Offices accounted for 29% of regional investment, followed by retail at 27%, residential at 19%, and industrial and logistics assets at 17%.

World.title: Romanian animated short film selected in UK’s Official Encounters Competition
World.content:
Happy New Year, the Romanian animated short film directed by Radu Gaciu and produced by Adriana Bumbeș through Ariadna Films, has been selected for the Official Competition of the Encounters Film Festival. The film will have its world premiere on September 23, 2026, at Watershed in Bristol.

The film, set in 2009 in Romania, follows a woman who returns home on her birthday to the isolated cabin in the mountains where she spent part of her youth with her twin sister. She rediscovers a space where memory and dreams intertwine and where echoes of the past speak of the pain of separation.

With a running time of 25 minutes, Happy New Year is a fantasy drama made using a mixed 2D digital animation technique.

Encounters is a qualifying festival for the BAFTA, BIFA and European Film Awards and also gives filmmakers the chance to enter the race for the Academy Awards, in the Best Animated Short Film category. The film is eligible for the Animated Encounters Grand Prix and the Audience Award.

The movie was built over five years of work, two years of pre-production and three years of production. The animation was based on more than 60,000 reference photographs, used to build the characters and backgrounds. The project brought together a team of more than 25 people, from actresses and screenwriters to production, sound and image specialists. The film’s visual universe was created from several thousand digitally made elements, characters and backgrounds, complemented by almost 100 unique watercolor paintings.

“The film’s animation technique is mixed, a combination of digital drawing, rotoscoping and collage, in which both the characters and the settings are stylistically rendered realistically. The characters are predominantly digital drawings that were later animated or, in a few cases, rotoscoped, also digitally. The backgrounds are complex collages of adjusted photographs composed with the help of additional graphic elements,” director Radu Gaciu said.

The lead role is voiced by Ana Ularu, one of the Romanian actresses with the most solid and visible international career. The voice cast is completed by Ana-Maria Guran, Clara Angela Roman and Oana Rotaru.

The project’s journey began at the Animest International Festival, where Happy New Year won the 2020 edition of the Pitch, Please! competition. The award took the project to the CEE Animation Forum 2021. The project continued its development and production in Romania, received production support from the National Cinematography Center, and was completed on January 31, 2026.

The film is produced by Ariadna Films. The screenplay is by Radu Gaciu and Nicoleta Colopelnic, while the producer is Adriana Bumbeș.

The film’s original music was specially composed by Matei Vasilache.

World.title: President Nicușor Dan to lead Romania’s delegation to UN General Assembly
World.content:
President Nicușor Dan will lead Romania’s delegation to the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, which will take place in New York next month, according to an announcement from the Presidential Administration.

The central theme of the next UN session is 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.'

The head of state will deliver the national statement in the plenary session of the UN General Assembly on September 23. He will highlight Romania’s efforts to support the organization’s reform process and the country’s contribution to ensuring peace, security and an international order based on rules and norms, according to the same source.

This is the first time president Nicușor Dan will attend the UN General Assembly. Last year, Romania was represented by foreign minister Oana Țoiu. Dan explained at the time that he did not go to New York because he considered it “more useful” to be present in the country.

At the next UN assembly, the president will also participate in New York in events organized on the sidelines of the high-level segment. He will hold bilateral meetings with other heads of state or government, including to support Romania’s candidacy for the leadership of the International Organisation of La Francophonie.

Former European Commissioner Dacian Cioloș is supported by Romania for the position of Secretary General of the OIF.
